title: Angle switch: carry ms position, no remount, keep play state and speed, pre-sign all angles
description:
Branch: feat/angle-switch-fix (worktree ~/code/EloRated/jits_web-wt-angle-switch). IN PROGRESS. Supersedes jits-n2im.20 (same scope, carried over with its acceptance).
BUG (verified at f28b164, apps/mobile/app/(app)/video/[id].tsx): onSelect computes translateAngleTime(...) then router.setParams({ id: other, t: String(Math.floor(moved.t)), ... }) (line 155), and the screen renders <PlayerBody key={id ?? 'none'} .../> (line 48). So a switch (a) throws away up to 999 ms (25-50x the 20-40 ms audio-sync accuracy) and (b) unmounts the player: new native player, new sign RPC, new load, resume seek, new telemetry session, playback rate reset to 1x and play/pause reset to autoplay.
FIX:
1. Carry the translated position in MILLISECONDS end to end (no Math.floor); set player.currentTime (frame-exact on both platforms) to the exact value.
2. Hold the active angle in screen state; stop keying PlayerBody on the video id (setParams only for deep links). One screen instance per match.
3. Preserve play/pause intent and playbackRate across the switch.
4. Sign ALL playable angles in one pass at screen open (re-sign together on expiry), so a switch never waits on a sign RPC. (Adopt jr_be-du1.3 shared URLs later.)
5. Update the stale comments that say nothing writes sync_offset_ms; read sync_source alongside the offset.
6. Keep one telemetry session across switches (minimal: do not end/start a session on switch; full switch telemetry is Player v1).
Still one player (swap + seek) in this slice; stacked players are Player v1.
SHIP: OTA (EAS Update), JS only, current runtime 0.5.0. No native change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Unit test: switching at t=30.000 s from the primary to an angle with offset +1500 ms seeks to exactly 28.500 s (no flooring) and keeps playing.
2. Test: paused stays paused; 0.5x stays 0.5x after a switch.
3. Test: no remount on switch (player instance and telemetry session survive), and no sign RPC is issued at switch time when the URL is fresh.
4. Shared contract fixture with jr_be (offset sign convention: sync_offset_ms(V) = start(V) - start(primary), primary = 0) passes.
5. Device check (iOS + Android): the same action is visible at the same moment after a switch on prod match bc093d63 (or a consented fixture).
6. Full jits_web gate green (typecheck, tests, expo export); independent review clean; shipped by OTA; /canvas-sync if any board changes.

title: Mobile: lobby presence channel killed by server rate limit is never re-joined; athlete shows LIVE but is invisible
description: Realtime v2.130 per-channel client_presence_rate_limit (5 calls / 30s). Over it the server closes the channel (ClientPresenceRateLimitReached, seen in local realtime logs at 04:53:01.941 for Demo Blue). apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-lobby-presence.ts subscribe callback handles only SUBSCRIBED; CLOSED/CHANNEL_ERROR/TIMED_OUT ignored; module channelRef keeps the dead channel; joinLobby -> trackDesired pushes into it and silently fails for the rest of the process. UI still shows LIVE / Go offline / You're in the lobby (use-arena-live writes the DB flag). title: Arena mobile: the roster only refreshes on pull
description:
Found in review of the Arena mobile branch (A11), and it is the enabling condition for the cap misattribution fixed in fbdc24e.

apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-arena-roster.ts fetches once on mount and then only when `refresh()` is called (pull-to-refresh, or the new onOpponentUnavailable path). There is no realtime subscription on `athletes` and no refetch on focus, so `acceptsRanked` and the roster membership itself are a snapshot that ages the whole time the screen is open. Presence keeps the Online/Open split honest for people who are IN the roster, but someone who goes live AFTER the snapshot never appears at all until a manual pull.

This is more visible now that the product keeps people live while they wander into profiles and matches: the Arena screen can stay mounted for a long time.

Options: refetch when the Arena tab regains selection (useIsTabSelected already computes it), a postgres_changes subscription on athletes filtered to looking_for_ranked, or a slow poll.
acceptance_criteria: An athlete who goes live while another athlete is already sitting on the Arena appears to them without a manual pull.
notes: Fix on branch fix/arena-roster-live: apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-roster-lobby-sync.ts quietly re-reads the roster when a lobby:online id is missing from it (1s coalesce, 3s min gap, one read in flight, each missing id tried once until the roster set changes or they leave the lobby) and once when the viewer goes live. Awaiting independent review and merge by the orchestrator.
close_reason: Merged (roster lobby sync); reviewed twice.

title: Accessibility token repair: fix the 6 failing contrast pairs and the invisible card edge (ships first, token-only)
description: The mobile app's most common text style fails WCAG AA in both themes, and cards are effectively invisible against the page. Verified by independent computation against the real token values in apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts. Dark theme (plate #1A1D24 on page #0D0F14): ink-3 #6B7280 on plate is 3.49:1, ink-on-cta #E8EDF2 on CTA #E63946 is 3.54:1, cta as text on plate is 4.05:1, plate vs page separation is 1.14:1. Light theme (plate #DEE2E9 on page #F2F4F7): ink-3 on plate is 3.72:1, cta as text on plate is 3.21:1, plate vs page is 1.18:1. ink-3 is the color of the single most common text style in the app, used at 10px in 163 places, so this is the highest-leverage defect in the codebase. The light hairline is also specified weaker (alpha 0.14) than the dark one (0.25), so the theme that needs the stronger edge has the weaker one. The user approved shipping this FIRST, ahead of the nav and Arena work, precisely because it is a token-only change with zero call sites: every screen built afterwards then inherits correct colors instead of needing a re-sweep. CRITICAL: do NOT change the brand red. The design proposal's remedy of deepening the CTA to #D22736 measures 4.37:1 and still fails AA (the proposal's claim of 5.14:1 is wrong). Keep accentCta #E63946 and darken the button LABEL to the existing Void token #0D0F14, which measures 4.60:1 and passes. That keeps app.json's push accent untouched and therefore needs no native rebuild. Token edits must land in all three hand-mirrored files or they will drift: apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js, apps/mobile/lib/tokens.ts, and apps/web/app/design-system/tokens.css. OTA: yes, fully OTA shippable, no native rebuild.
design: Direction A (Instrument) as approved by the user. Fix execution, not identity. Label-darkening is preferred over brand-red deepening specifically because it keeps the change OTA-only.

title: P0: recording maxDuration 600s races the match clock, truncating the clip and uploading mid-match
description:
GAP 2. WHY THIS IS P0: it silently loses the end of every full-length match, which is the part people most want to watch.

THE DEFECT: `maxDuration` is 600s (`lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:277`), EXACTLY equal to the default `matches.duration_seconds` of 600. But recording starts AFTER the match starts: there is up to a 3s camera-ready backstop plus up to 8s of not-ready retries, and pauses extend wall-clock time further. So on any full-length match the OS cap fires BEFORE the match ends. That hits the "settled without an explicit stop" branch, which UPLOADS the truncated clip mid-match, and the later real stop() then no-ops. The final minutes are never captured and nothing tells the user.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- The recording cap can no longer expire before a match of the configured duration ends. Give the cap real headroom over `matches.duration_seconds` rather than matching it, and account for the start delay and for pause time.
- If the OS cap DOES fire (it is a backstop, it must still be handled), it must not be treated as a normal completion: the user is told the recording hit its limit, and the later real stop must not silently no-op into nothing.
- Derive the cap from the match's duration where that is knowable rather than hardcoding a second magic number that will drift from the backend default the same way this one did.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update).
acceptance_criteria: A 10-minute match on device produces a single clip covering the whole match including the final minute, uploaded once, after the match ends. Forcing the OS cap produces a clear user-facing message and no silent truncation. A regression test asserts the cap is strictly greater than the match duration plus the worst-case start delay. Verified on physical hardware, not just in the simulator.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-18 on branch impl-video-p0, commit 37e52ec. Cap derived in apps/mobile/lib/video/recording-limits.ts from matches.duration_seconds plus a 600s pause allowance plus a start/stop budget computed from the recorder's own retry constants (14s), clamped to [900, 7200]. A 600s match now caps at 1214s instead of 600s. The backstop firing is classified (limit vs interrupted, from the elapsed recording wall-clock) and surfaced through UploadProgressBanner instead of passing as a plain success; a stop arriving after it logs instead of no-opping silently. The viewfinder also mounts from the READY step so the capture session is warm before start_match. STILL NEEDS PHYSICAL HARDWARE: the simulator has no camera, so the 10-minute end-to-end recording in the AC is unverified. Awaiting independent review; not closed.
REVIEW ROUND 2, commit 3b8e97f. Two lifecycle defects the hoist introduced or exposed, both fixed: (F2) the recorder now outlives the viewfinder, so the 3s camera-ready backstop fired against a null cameraRef when a match ended inside it, hitting 'Camera not ready' and, because the status chip is persistent, accusing the user of a camera failure through result, confirm and summary. The backstop now checks the ref and MatchRecorderCamera calls a new releaseCamera() on unmount. (F3) 'stopping' had NO exit: issuePendingStop gives up after 2s and the machine sat in stopping forever, which since the hoist also pinned a live viewfinder and a lit iOS mic indicator over the result and summary steps. Added STOP_WATCHDOG_MS (10s, derived from the re-issue budget plus 8s of finalize slack) that releases the camera and reports that the recording did not finish. Also closed the PRE-EXISTING dead end where recordAsync settling with no URI while not stopping returned with no transition at all, leaving the machine stranded in 'recording': the one path where the cap could fire and the user was told nothing.
N5 from the b5b7d8c review, no action needed, recorded so it is not re-reported as a defect. On a near-2 GiB clip whose native finalize takes longer than the 8s of slack in STOP_WATCHDOG_MS (10s total = the 2s stop re-issue budget + 8s), the watchdog can fire and flash 'The recording did not finish' before recordAsync settles and the chip self-corrects to 'Uploading...'. It self-heals, the clip is still uploaded (stoppingRef is deliberately left true so a late settle takes the normal stopped path), and it is vastly better than the infinite spinner with a pinned camera and lit mic indicator that it replaced. If it ever proves annoying on real hardware, scale the slack with the recorded duration rather than raising the flat 8s.
close_reason: Merged to development as b5b7d8c. Review rejected the first attempt: it routed the fix through component state, and refresh() at confirm-to-summary unmounted the recorder on EVERY match, so videoId, the chip and any failure were destroyed regardless of upload timing. The shipped fix keys the upload outcome on matchId in a module-scope store written with no mounted guard, so it survives a provider remount, a step transition, and an upload completing after the recorder is gone. Verified robust rather than layered: deleting the accompanying revalidating predicate leaves all five regression tests green, and all five are proven red against the pre-fix commit. maxDuration is now derived from the retry constants (1214s for a 600s match) with those constants moved beside it. NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE: the simulator has no camera.

title: Decouple MatchFlowWizard from the required sessionId (exitHref / exitLabel / allowTimekeeper)
description:
WAVE 1a. THIS SHIPS FIRST AND ALONE. Both Arena and the video hardening build on it.

WHY: `apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-flow-wizard.tsx:17` takes `sessionId` as a REQUIRED prop, and the only thing it is used for is exit navigation. Four hardcoded redirects assume a session lobby:
- `steps/ready-step.tsx:62` and `:117`
- `steps/summary-step.tsx:168`
- `components/match-flow/wizard-status.tsx:48`
all of them `router.replace('/(app)/session/${sessionId}/lobby')`. The prop is threaded through `match-flow-wizard.tsx:17,59,111` and `match-step-renderer.tsx:28,50,87,163`.

An Arena match has no session, so as long as this prop is required there is no way to run one. The backend already permits a sessionless match: `chk_match_origin` is `CHECK (challenge_id IS NOT NULL OR session_id IS NOT NULL)` (jr_be migration 20260405000600_matches_session_support.sql:54-56) and `matches.session_id` is nullable. The blocker is purely the mobile client's prop contract.

This is EXACTLY the coupling web had before 5b90ff1, and web already solved it: it replaced `sessionId` with an `exitHref` / `exitLabel` pair plus an `allowTimekeeper` flag. Mobile does the same refactor. Read the web change first and mirror its shape so the two platforms do not diverge.

WHAT DONE MEANS:
- `sessionId` is no longer a required prop of MatchFlowWizard. Callers pass `exitHref` (where Done / Back goes) and `exitLabel` (the button copy), plus `allowTimekeeper`.
- All four hardcoded `router.replace` sites use `exitHref`.
- `sessionId` is removed from the threading in match-step-renderer where it was only carrying exit intent. If a step genuinely needs the session id for data (not navigation), keep it, but as an optional prop, and say so in the PR.
- The existing session entry point (`/(app)/session/[id]/lobby`) passes `exitHref` for the session lobby and `exitLabel` "Back to Lobby", so session matches behave exactly as they do today.
- While in here: `wait` in `lib/match-flow/step-router.ts:20-39` is unreachable dead code. Note it, do not necessarily delete it in this change, file a follow-up if removal is not trivially safe.

DO NOT in this issue: add the Arena route, add video changes, or change any step's behavior. This is a navigation-contract refactor only, and it is deliberately small so it can land fast and unblock two parallel workstreams.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.
design:
Mirror web's 5b90ff1 prop shape exactly rather than inventing a mobile-specific one: `exitHref`, `exitLabel`, `allowTimekeeper`. Divergent prop names across platforms is how the two match flows drift apart, and the match flow is the single most correctness-sensitive screen in the product.

`allowTimekeeper` exists because a session match has a third party (the gym running the session) who can operate the clock, while a peer-to-peer Arena match does not. Carry the flag even if mobile does not branch on it yet, so the contract is stable when it does.
acceptance_criteria: MatchFlowWizard compiles and runs with no `sessionId` prop. A session match started from the session lobby completes end to end and Done returns to the session lobby with the label "Back to Lobby", identical to today. A wizard mounted with an arbitrary `exitHref` returns there instead. No `router.replace('/(app)/session/...')` string literal remains in the match-flow tree. Unit tests cover exit routing for both a session exit and a non-session exit. Mobile typecheck and test suite are green.
notes: TRAP FOR WHOEVER DOES ARENA (jits-54km): allowTimekeeper was deliberately NOT added to mobile in this change, because mobile has zero timekeeper branches (all nine 'timekeeper' hits in apps/mobile are comments; step-router collapses the variants, the step renderer has no branch, and the session lobby creates matches with no timekeeper_id). If it is ever added, it MUST default to TRUE, matching web's default at apps/web/app/(app)/session/[id]/match/[matchId]/match-flow-content.tsx:39. A false default would silently change session match semantics, since web uses allowTimekeeper to gate isTimekeeper, hasTimekeeper and timekeeperEnabled all at once.
close_reason: Merged to development as fd2ae38. Independently reviewed, two defects found and fixed (exit-guard bypass on the group-less route spelling, blank exitLabel rendering an unlabeled CTA), both proven closed by mutation. Session path verified byte-identical. Gate green on the merged result.

title: [epic] Match with video on prod: record, upload, watch (no analysis)
description:
WAVE 2b. Depends on the wizard decoupling (1a). Runs in parallel with Arena.

SCOPE, AND THE BOUNDARY MATTERS: this targets PROD and is record, upload, watch ONLY. NO AI analysis, no slicing, no Cloud Run, no edge functions, no analysis UI. The jits-kaf tree owns the analysis pipeline and is NOT in scope here. Where the two touch the same file, this epic is a prerequisite: analysis of a clip that was never captured or never uploaded is meaningless.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS: the happy path exists and has been verified on hardware once. expo-camera CameraView mounted on the live step (`steps/live-step.tsx:67`, `:135`), recording 720p MP4 H.264/AAC via `lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:125`. Upload is a single-shot `FileSystem.uploadAsync` BINARY_CONTENT POST straight to `storage/v1/object/match-videos/<match_id>/<uploader_athlete_id>/<ts>.mp4` (`lib/video/upload-recording.ts`), a path convention that matches the prod storage RLS exactly, followed by `upsertMatchVideo` writing the row with status 'ready'. Playback is `apps/mobile/app/(app)/video/[id].tsx` on expo-av, resolving via `getMatchVideoSignedUrl` (queries.ts:1829) which prefers `normalized_path` then `storage_path`. Mobile records MP4 so normalized_path is null and storage_path is signed, which is correct on prod.

WHAT IS BROKEN: eleven verified gaps, filed as children. Two are P0 because they lose footage or lose all user feedback: the upload UI unmounts the instant the upload starts, and the OS recording cap fires BEFORE a full-length match ends and uploads a truncated clip mid-match.

NOT A RISK, do not treat it as one: oversize. The 2 GiB client cap matches the prod bucket limit and is unreachable at 720p for 600s. It is filed as a correct-error-message issue, not a P0.

TEST BASELINE: existing coverage is `apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/video/upload-recording.test.ts` (9 cases), `use-video-recorder.test.ts` (13 cases), `step-router.test.ts`, `ready-step.test.tsx`, plus packages/shared `match-video.test.ts` and `athlete-videos.test.ts`. NOT covered: LiveStep, CameraOverlay, UploadProgressBanner, video/[id].tsx, PastMatchVideos, the normalized_path preference, and the whole record-upload-watch sequence. There is no mobile e2e harness at all.

DELIVERY: every child is OTA-safe (EAS Update). expo-camera, expo-av, expo-file-system and expo-video-thumbnails are all already installed. If a fix needs a package that is not, it becomes a native rebuild and comes back to the user first.
acceptance_criteria: On prod, on physical hardware: a full-length (10 minute) match records end to end without truncation, the user sees upload state from the moment the match ends through to success or failure on every subsequent wizard step, a failed upload can be retried manually and survives an app restart, backgrounding mid-record or mid-upload does not lose the clip, and the finished video is watchable directly from the match summary. Playback failures state their actual reason. Test coverage exists for the full sequence.
notes: PM 2026-10-04: remaining upload/record work continues under video overhaul epic jits-n2im (client) / jr_be-1qz (backend).

title: [epic] Mobile native build: nav surgery, Arena, video hardening, style refresh
description:
PROGRAM EPIC. Four mobile-only workstreams, sequenced. The web half of this work already shipped on `development` at 5b90ff1 (Gyms out of web primary nav, /arena and /arena/swipe un-hidden, /arena/match/[matchId] added, instant challenge handshake hook, Arena on brand tokens). MOBILE WAS NOT TOUCHED. Nothing in this epic re-specs web.

WHY: mobile is the priority surface (see the `native-first-then-web-rollout` memory) and it is currently missing the product's headline social loop. There is no Arena on mobile at all: no route, no lobby presence, no way to issue a challenge, just a disabled button on the athlete profile. At the same time the tab bar carries two gym tabs (one of them manager-gated) that crowd out Arena, and the match video path has eleven verified defects including two that lose footage outright.

BUILD ORDER (encoded as real dependency edges, not prose):
- WAVE 1a, ALONE AND FIRST: decouple MatchFlowWizard from its required `sessionId` prop. Everything else builds on it.
- WAVE 1b, parallel with 1a: navigation surgery (4-up tab bar, gym and session discovery onto Home, manager entry relocated onto /gyms/[id], manager ROUTES kept alive).
- WAVE 2a: Arena (depends on 1a and 1b).
- WAVE 2b: match-with-video hardening (depends on 1a).
- WAVE 3: style refresh, gated on the user approving a design direction first.

SETTLED DECISIONS, DO NOT REOPEN:
- Both mobile gym tabs come out. The bar becomes Home, Arena, Rankings, Profile.
- Gym and session entry moves to the Home dashboard.
- Arena on mobile gets full parity with web PLUS a swipe surface.
- Match-with-video targets PROD and is record, upload, watch ONLY. No AI analysis, no slicing, no Cloud Run, no edge functions. The jits-kaf tree covers analysis and is explicitly NOT in scope here.
- Delivery is local `expo run:ios --device` builds plus EAS Update OTA. No EAS cloud builds and no TestFlight release without the user's explicit go. See the delivery gate child issue.
- Style work needs an approved design direction before any style code is written.

SCOPE BOUNDARY vs jits-kaf: jits-kaf is the full video integration epic including the chunked AI analysis pipeline. This program owns only the client-side record/upload/watch reliability on mobile. Where the two touch the same file, this program's issues win on sequencing because they are prerequisites for anything analysis-related working at all.
design:
OTA vs NATIVE REBUILD LEDGER for this program. Every child issue carries its own one-line classification; this is the summary.

OTA-SAFE (the overwhelming majority): all navigation work (the tab bar and every app header are custom JS), the whole Arena feature, every video-path fix listed here, font swaps (fonts load at runtime via @expo-google-fonts with NO expo-font config plugin), icon swaps (lucide-react-native over already-linked react-native-svg), and every token or className change.

NEEDS A NATIVE REBUILD: the native splash (app.json:96-102), the app icon (app.json:7) and Android adaptive icon (app.json:44-47), the push accent color (app.json:120-124), `userInterfaceStyle`, `edgeToEdgeEnabled`, and any new native dependency at all.

RUNTIME VERSION TRAP: `runtimeVersion.policy` is "appVersion" (app.json:10), so an OTA update only reaches binaries at the same version, currently 0.2.0. Bumping `expo.version` as part of a JS-only release would ORPHAN the update: it would never reach the installed builds. Do not bump the version for an OTA release.
acceptance_criteria: All four workstream epics are closed, the mobile quality gate (typecheck plus the test suite plus expo export) is green, and the app has been exercised on physical hardware through: Home to gym to session, Arena to challenge to match to video, and back. No EAS cloud build or TestFlight submission has happened without an explicit user go.
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-10-06 REOPENS the settled 4-up tab bar: the mobile bar becomes FIVE tabs, Home, Arena, Matches, Rankings, Profile. The new Matches tab holds the athlete's own match history (reel carousel + filter chips + YouTube-style match feed) and replaces the pushed Film Room screen; Profile drops Recent Matches, HighlightsRow and the Film Room preview; Home gets a Your reels carousel. Epic jits-a4fw, spec specs/matches-tab/spec.md. The (tabs)/_layout.tsx comment 'target 4-up' is updated by jits-a4fw.3.
2026-10-06: the 5-tab bar (Home, Arena, Matches, Rankings, Profile) shipped in production OTA be389c6c-e64e-4493-ac33-e54ca9fcf905 (epic jits-a4fw), superseding the 4-tab decision on mobile; web keeps four tabs.

title: [bug] Web recording is dead on Safari/iOS and reports 'Camera access denied'
description:
PROBLEM: apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts picks a mimeType from a WebM-only preference list (:171-172: vp9 -> vp8 -> video/webm) with a '?? "video/webm"' fallback. Safari's MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported returns false for EVERY WebM type, so .find() returns undefined and the unsupported fallback string is handed to 'new MediaRecorder(stream, { mimeType })' at :173, which throws NotSupportedError.

That constructor sits INSIDE the same try whose catch at :195-196 sets 'Camera access denied. You can still manage the match without video.' So on Safari/iOS the recorder never starts AND the user is told it is a camera-permission problem. Anyone debugging this will chase permissions indefinitely.

Impact: no web user on Safari (all iOS browsers, plus macOS Safari) can record a match at all. Silent for us, misleading for them.

FIX:
1. Probe 'video/mp4' FIRST (Safari supports MediaRecorder video/mp4; modern Chromium does too), then fall back to the WebM list.
2. Never construct MediaRecorder with a type that isTypeSupported rejected - if nothing is supported, fail with an explicit 'This browser cannot record video' message.
3. Split the try/catch: getUserMedia failure => permission/device message; MediaRecorder construction failure => codec message. They are different faults and must not share copy.
4. Derive the stored file extension and blob type from the ACTUAL recorder.mimeType rather than the hardcoded 'webm' at :84 and :151.

Item 4 overlaps jits-kaf.1.2 (the WebM-vs-MP4 container decision); items 1-3 are worth shipping regardless of which container option is chosen.

DISCOVERED BY: adversarial audit of the video upload path, 2026-09-10. Verified by code reading (Safari not directly tested from this machine).

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-11 (jits_web, uncommitted; pending independent review).

apps/web/lib/video/recorder-codec.ts (NEW, pure + unit-tested):
- MIME_PREFERENCE now leads with MP4/H.264 ('video/mp4;codecs="avc1.42E01E"' -> avc1 -> video/mp4) before the WebM list. Fixes Safari, and per jits-kaf.1.2 option A an H.264 source is also the only container that survives the slicer's '-c copy' fast path untouched.

apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts:
- startRecording() split into two try blocks: a getUserMedia failure keeps the 'Camera access denied' copy; a codec failure now says "This browser can't record video" / "Couldn't start the recorder on this browser" and logs the real error. The two faults no longer share copy.
- When pickMimeType() returns null the stream is released and we bail with an honest message instead of constructing MediaRecorder with an unsupported type.
- Upload path uses recorder.mimeType (authoritative; the browser may hand back a different type than requested) for BOTH the storage contentType and the extension.
- Added upsert:true so a retry against the same path replaces rather than 409s (partial jits-od3).
- stopRecording() now stops the camera tracks inside onstop, AFTER the final dataavailable has flushed. Previously they were stopped synchronously alongside recorder.stop(), which can truncate the last chunk.
- 'catch { fail("Upload failed") }' now preserves and logs the underlying error; we were blind in the field.

Gate: typecheck clean all 3 workspaces; 257 tests pass (web 45->56); eslint clean on touched files.

title: video-webhook auto-triggers legacy whole-video analyzer and wins the race, killing the chunked path
acceptance_criteria: A video that reaches status='ready' is sliced by the chunked pipeline (status walks ready -> slicing -> analyzing -> merging -> analyzed) and the legacy whole-video video-analyze function is NOT invoked. The slicer no longer logs 'slice skipped: status not ready' for a freshly-ready video. If the legacy path is kept behind a flag, the flag defaults to OFF and there is a test asserting the default.

title: Slicer aborts every chunk analysis at 30s: ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS far below analyzer budget
description:
All code cited lives in the jr_be repo (~/code/EloRated/jr_be) unless noted.

The Cloud Run slicer aborts every chunk-analysis POST at 30 seconds, which is far shorter than the analyzer's own budget, so no chunk analysis can ever complete through the normal fan-out path.

Evidence:
- `workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:114` sets the fan-out timeout default:
  `const ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = Number(process.env.ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 30_000);`
  The comment above it (main.js:112-113) claims "The Edge Function has its own internal timeouts; this is just to keep one slow chunk from pinning the worker". That assumption is wrong, see below.
- `workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:711` uses that value as a hard AbortController deadline on the POST:
  `const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS);` inside `postAnalyze(url, chunkId)` (declared at main.js:709).
- `video-analyze-chunk` is fully synchronous. It does the Gemini work inside the request and only responds when analysis is done. Its own budgets are `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_MS_STANDARD = 60_000` and `GEMINI_TIMEOUT_MS_PREMIUM = 300_000` at `supabase/functions/video-analyze-chunk/index.ts:137-138`, plus up to roughly 150s of Gemini File API upload/poll before the model call even starts (`supabase/functions/video-analyze-chunk/index.ts:149-150`).

So worst case the analyzer legitimately needs about 150s + 300s = 450s for premium and about 150s + 60s = 210s for standard, while the slicer gives it 30s. The slicer aborts the connection on essentially every chunk.

Interaction with jits-ayj (do not duplicate that bug, it is a different defect): an AbortController abort DOES reject the fetch promise, so unlike the HTTP-status bug in jits-ayj these aborts land in the `failed` bucket of `fanOutAnalyze()`. With all chunks failing, the worker returns 500 and pg_net does not retry, so the video is stranded. Fixing jits-ayj alone will not fix this; fixing this alone will not fix jits-ayj.

Fix shape (either is acceptable):
1. Raise the `ANALYZE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` default to >= 420000 (7 minutes) so it exceeds the premium-tier worst case, and set the matching env var on the deployed Cloud Run service; or
2. Make the fan-out fire-and-forget (dispatch the POST without awaiting the analysis body) and rely on the chunk state machine plus the reaper/retry sweep for completion tracking. Note this changes what the worker can report about success/failure, so coordinate with jits-ayj's success/failure accounting fix.

Also update the stale comment at `workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:112-113`, which asserts the Edge Function's internal timeouts make this a mere safety net.
acceptance_criteria: A standard-tier chunk analysis completes without the slicer aborting the connection: postAnalyze() holds the connection long enough for video-analyze-chunk to return its result, the chunk lands in status 'completed', and the worker reports it as a success. Verified end-to-end against a real (non-trivial) chunk, not a stub. Premium-tier worst case (~450s) is also covered by whatever deadline is chosen, or the fan-out is fire-and-forget so no client-side deadline applies. The stale comment at workers/video-slicer/src/main.js:112-113 is corrected.

title: Persistent upload status indicator across match wizard steps (signals + retry)
description:
Requested by product owner during the 2026-06-10 on-device test, where it was impossible to tell from the phone whether the match recording uploaded. Today UploadProgressBanner lives only inside the live step; the moment the wizard advances to result/confirm/summary, all upload visibility vanishes, and a failed/stuck upload is invisible (also makes field debugging blind).

Spec: lift recorder/upload state out of live-step (wizard-level context or a small upload-manager module in apps/mobile/lib/video/) and render a compact persistent status chip on the result, confirm, and summary steps: recording / uploading / saved (with checkmark) / failed (with Retry CTA that re-runs uploadRecording against the SAME storage path). No percentage bar: FileSystem.uploadAsync emits no progress events for BINARY_CONTENT; state-based signals only (note resumable TUS upload as the future path to real progress). Animation must follow brand motion rules (reactive status spinner like the existing banner; no decorative motion). Also surfaces the diagnostic [video] log tags in dev. Mirrors web later (web has the same gap after match-recorded-step unmounts).
acceptance_criteria: After ending a match, every wizard step until summary shows the upload state; a failed upload shows Retry and retrying reuses the same storage path; success shows confirmation; covered by component tests for all four states.
notes:
ADOPTED 2026-09-18 into the mobile native build program (epic jits-tj5n, video epic jits-5tj9) as GAP 1, the worst defect in the record-upload-watch path. Bumped P1 -> P0 and reparented under the video epic.

WHY IT IS P0: the upload UI unmounts the moment the upload starts. UploadProgressBanner lives INSIDE LiveStep (live-step.tsx:155). Ending the match stops the recorder and calls onEnded in the same tick, LiveStep unmounts, and the upload begins AFTER that. So the user never sees uploading, never sees success, and never sees failure. Every other video fix in this epic is invisible to the user until this one lands: retry has nowhere to render its CTA, progress has nowhere to render its percentage, and a failed upload stays silent.

ALSO DEAD STATE: recorder.videoId (use-video-recorder.ts:439) has ZERO consumers. It is set and never read. Either wire it into the persistent state this issue introduces, or delete it; do not leave it.

DEPENDENCIES ADDED: blocked by the MatchFlowWizard sessionId decoupling (jits-3929), because both refactor the wizard's cross-step contract and doing them independently guarantees a conflict. This issue in turn blocks real upload progress (jits-l5eq), manual retry and persistence (jits-341p), and the sequence test coverage (jits-1yp1).

NOTE ON PROGRESS: the original spec correctly said no percentage bar, because FileSystem.uploadAsync with BINARY_CONTENT emits no progress events. That constraint is now addressed separately in jits-l5eq by moving to FileSystem.createUploadTask, which does expose progress. Build the state-based signals here; the percentage lands on top of them there.

DELIVERY: OTA-safe (EAS Update). JS only.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-18 on branch impl-video-p0, commit 37e52ec (worktree .claude/worktrees/impl-video-p0). Recorder hoisted into MatchRecorderProvider (components/match-flow/match-recorder-context.tsx) above the step boundary; the status chip and the viewfinder are rendered by the wizard via match-recorder-surface.tsx. recorder.videoId now feeds a Watch Match Video action on the summary step, so jits-p75q's first half is covered here too. NOT DONE, deliberately out of scope per the implementation brief: the Retry CTA and the persisted file URI, which stay with jits-341p. The hoisted state is shaped so a retry action can be added without moving it again. Awaiting independent review; not closed.
REVIEW ROUND 2, commit 3b8e97f on impl-video-p0 (merged development e6ec219 first). Review of 37e52ec found the hoist alone was NOT enough: the wizard remounts on EVERY match, because the confirm step calls refresh() when the row goes terminal and useMatchDetails re-enters loading above the provider. That destroyed videoId, the success chip and the failure message deterministically, not as a race. Mobile was therefore strictly worse than apps/web, which loses its videoId only in a race window. FIX: match-scoped upload store at apps/mobile/lib/video/match-upload-store.ts, keyed on matchId, read via useSyncExternalStore; the recorder writes the outcome there unguarded by mountedRef. Closes the remount AND the late-completing-upload case that still defeats web. apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-banner-state.ts holds the precedence between the view-bound recorder and the durable store as one pure tested table. The wizard also no longer re-enters its loading branch for a revalidation of a match it already holds. The web session has offered to mirror this store; nothing was put in packages/shared. Retry is still jits-341p and the hook still needs lastFileUriRef plus a retry() for it (see correction on that issue). Awaiting re-review; not closed.
close_reason: Merged to development as b5b7d8c. Review rejected the first attempt: it routed the fix through component state, and refresh() at confirm-to-summary unmounted the recorder on EVERY match, so videoId, the chip and any failure were destroyed regardless of upload timing. The shipped fix keys the upload outcome on matchId in a module-scope store written with no mounted guard, so it survives a provider remount, a step transition, and an upload completing after the recorder is gone. Verified robust rather than layered: deleting the accompanying revalidating predicate leaves all five regression tests green, and all five are proven red against the pre-fix commit. maxDuration is now derived from the retry constants (1214s for a 600s match) with those constants moved beside it. NOT VERIFIED ON HARDWARE: the simulator has no camera.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text:
WEB HALF: the mobile design has landed and web should mirror it rather than invent a second one. Recording the shape here so it is not lost in a session transcript. Source: jr-be-73 session, 2026-09-19, mirrored back after I sent them the web comparison.

WEB'S CURRENT STATE IS DIFFERENT FROM MOBILE'S, and milder, but broken in the same way at the end.
- videoId is already WIZARD-level, not step-level: match-flow-wizard.tsx:38 holds it, the recorder lives in steps/timekeeper-live-step.tsx:36, and the id is lifted via handleNext (wizard:44) into match-summary (:73) and match-recorded (:75). So a step unmount does NOT destroy it.
- BUT the lift only happens ON ADVANCE. apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts deliberately lets the storage upload and the match_videos write finish after unmount, guarding only React state writes behind mountedRef, so setVideoId is skipped once the step is gone. If the athlete advances before the upload completes, the row IS written and the id NEVER reaches the wizard: summary and recorded render with no video although the video exists in storage.
- Severity note: web's window is bounded by upload duration vs tap speed, so it looks intermittent in testing and is near-certain on a slow gym connection with a short match. Mobile's was unconditional (use-match-completion refetches on completed OR disputed plus a 1s timer when the row is already terminal at mount), so EVERY mobile match hit it. Mobile really was strictly worse; that is now confirmed rather than assumed.

MOBILE DESIGN TO MIRROR (apps/mobile/lib/video/):
1. match-upload-store.ts, ~160 lines, no deps beyond React. Module-scope Map<matchId, entry> + listener Set. Entry { matchId, status: pending|uploading|uploaded|error, videoId, error, truncation, storagePath, updatedAt }. setMatchUpload(matchId, patch) merges and ALWAYS replaces the entry object so a useSyncExternalStore snapshot compares unequal exactly when something changed. Reads via getMatchUpload(matchId) and useMatchUpload(matchId) over useSyncExternalStore, which reads correctly on FIRST RENDER even when the write happened before the component existed. In-memory, dies with the JS context (persistence is a separate issue). Entries NOT cleared on success or failure, because a visible failure is correct. Bounded MAX_TRACKED_MATCHES = 8, oldest-by-updatedAt eviction. storagePath recorded so a retry reuses the same key; the temp file URI deliberately not held.
2. upload-banner-state.ts, a PURE deriveUploadBannerState(recorderState, recorderError, upload) with its own test. Precedence: recorder-stopping first, then the STORE's outcome, then recorder-only failures (no camera, no permission, stop watchdog), then hidden. Their note: trusting the recorder over the store in that middle slot is what made the failure silent, so it is one table with one test rather than conditions scattered through a component.

THE CRITICAL LINE FOR WEB: the store write must be UNGUARDED BY ANY MOUNTED CHECK. That single property is what fixes web's bug, because web's upload already completes; it is the React state write that is skipped.

AND DELETE, DO NOT ADD: mobile removed setVideoId, setTruncation and their mountedRef guards entirely and derives both from the store. The web equivalent is removing the wizard-level videoId useState (match-flow-wizard.tsx:38) and the handleNext lift (:44) rather than keeping them alongside a store. Two sources of truth with a precedence rule between them is how this bug survives a refactor.

SCOPE WARNING: the mobile store lives in apps/mobile/lib/video/ and deliberately NOT in packages/shared, to avoid colliding with concurrent queries.ts work. A web version should sit in apps/web/lib/video/ for the same reason unless someone deliberately unifies them later.

NOT STARTED ON WEB. Waiting on the user; other work is queued ahead of it.

title: Deploy + wire the video analysis pipeline: slicer Cloud Run, video_slicer_url GUC, bucket in migration
description:
The pipeline exists in code but is almost certainly not running: the slicer dispatch silently NO-OPs when the app.settings.video_slicer_url GUC is unset, and the Cloud Run worker (jr_be/workers/video-slicer, 1051-line ffmpeg slicer) is likely not deployed. Also, the match-videos bucket exists only in supabase/config.toml, not in a migration, so a prod db push would not create it (prod-push risk).

Work (repo: jr_be):
1. Deploy workers/video-slicer to Cloud Run (follow the worker's own README/specs under jr_be/specs/013-chunked-video-pipeline if present); capture the service URL and auth.
2. Set the app.settings.video_slicer_url GUC (and any companion auth GUC) in each target environment; document where it is set (migration vs dashboard vs infra script) so it is not lost on db reset.
3. Move match-videos bucket creation (+ its storage policies) into a migration so prod push creates it; keep config.toml in sync for local dev.
4. Verify the Gemini analyze-chunk + merge edge functions are deployed and the pg_cron sweeps are scheduled.
5. End-to-end verification: insert/upload a real video, watch status walk ready→slicing→analyzing→merging→analyzed, and confirm get_video_analysis returns a payload (web timekeeper viewer or use-video-progress hook can be the probe).
6. Run npm run db:types in jits_web if any migration changed schema.
acceptance_criteria: A freshly-uploaded real video reaches status='analyzed' in a deployed environment with no manual poking. Bucket + policies are migration-managed (supabase db reset locally still creates them). GUC wiring documented. pgTAP suite green.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: Local portion done in jr_be (uncommitted, working tree): migration supabase/migrations/20260610000000_match_videos_bucket.sql + test supabase/tests/043_match_videos_bucket_test.sql (19 pgTAP tests). Bucket: idempotent INSERT INTO storage.buckets ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE, private, 2GiB limit (prod intent; local config.toml re-applies 500MiB after migrations on db reset, observed and documented in SQL comment), mime types video/mp4+quicktime+webm+x-msvideo+image/jpeg+png. Policies on storage.objects TO authenticated, path verified against buildMatchVideoStoragePath (<match_id>/<uploader_athlete_id>/<unix_ts>.<ext>, NO matches/ prefix) and slicer chunks subpath: match_videos_insert (own folder segment 2 = auth_athlete_id() AND participant of match in segment 1), match_videos_update + match_videos_delete (own folder, covers x-upsert retry + orphan-compensation remove()), match_videos_select (any participant of match in segment 1, mirrors match_videos_select_participant). Reused auth_athlete_id(); is_match_video_participant()/is_video_visible() NOT usable here (they key on match_videos.id which does not exist yet at upload time and is not in the path; is_video_visible also has EXECUTE revoked from authenticated). Verified signed-URL creation IS gated by the SELECT policy on storage-api v1.37.7 via live local API probe (13/13 checks: upsert re-upload 200, cross-folder upload 400, participant sign 200, outsider sign 400, non-owner delete 400, owner delete 200). Quality gate green: clean supabase db reset + supabase test db = 43 files / 1324 tests PASS (1305 pre-existing + 19 new). No public-schema change, so jits_web db:types regen not needed. Remains blocked on deployment: supabase db push to prod (creates bucket + policies remotely), slicer Cloud Run deploy, video_slicer_url GUC, edge function deploys, e2e prod verification (other parts of this bead).

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: LOCAL E2E VERIFICATION: PASS (2026-06-10). Proven on local stack: authenticated upload (storage RLS as real user JWT, x-upsert), match_videos INSERT RLS, AFTER INSERT trigger, pg_net delivery to host.docker.internal:8791, HMAC shared-secret auth (pos+neg), claim RPC, signed-URL download, ffmpeg copy-path slice, chunk upload, persist RPC atomic status flip (ready->slicing->analyzing, 289ms for 15s clip), idempotent replay, 4 cron sweeps registered. Parks at status='analyzing' without Gemini (expected; edge functions not running). UNVERIFIED: Gemini chunk analysis, merge path, re-encode path. Worker bug found and filed separately (fan-out 503s counted as success). Remaining for this issue: prod deploy (Cloud Run + GUCs + db push + GEMINI_API_KEY), blocked on credentials/go-ahead.

title: Phase 1 (Foundation): upload-path bug fixes + analysis pipeline deployed and verified
description:
Make the existing record→upload→analyze path reliable and actually running before building any UI on top of it.

Scope: the 6 open upload bugs (re-parented under this issue: jits-1v6, jits-81l, jits-hu0, jits-voh, jits-0lc, jits-za8), pipeline deployment/verification (slicer Cloud Run deploy + GUC wiring + bucket-in-migration), and the WebM-vs-MP4 decision for web recordings. Related: jits-a8y.13 (clip silently dropped if End fires before recorder reaches recording) stays under epic jits-a8y but is dep-linked here; fix it with this cluster.

Repos: jits_web (apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts, apps/mobile/lib/video/*, packages/shared/src/api/mutations.ts) + jr_be (workers/video-slicer, supabase/migrations, config.toml).
acceptance_criteria: All child/dep-linked bugs closed. A real mobile recording uploads (including the retry path), produces a match_videos row, and progresses ready→slicing→analyzing→merging→analyzed end-to-end against the deployed slicer. WebM decision recorded and its follow-up filed.

title: Mobile sign-in always redirects already-active athlete to /profile-setup (isLoading race)
description:
SYMPTOM: signing into the native app (Google SSO and email/password) always routes an already-active athlete to /profile-setup, which then renders in 'Edit Profile' mode with their info pre-filled. Confirmed on remote (prod rzowigdcdojlovlwwpkx) account matthew.spon@gmail.com: athletes row status=active, all fields populated. So backend data + triggers are correct; this is purely frontend.

ROOT CAUSE: apps/mobile/lib/auth/auth-context.tsx onAuthStateChange set isLoading=false in the no-user branch but never re-armed isLoading=true on a fresh sign-in. After sitting on the login screen (isLoading already false from INITIAL_SESSION no-user, athlete null), an explicit sign-in set user but left isLoading=false + athlete=null. login.tsx then router.replace('/'), and app/index.tsx ran 'if (!athlete) redirect(/profile-setup)' synchronously, before the async getCurrentAthlete resolved. Synchronous redirect beats async fetch every time -> happens on every sign-in, deterministically. Cold-start with a restored session was unaffected (INITIAL_SESSION arrives WITH a user; isLoading stays true until load).

FIX: re-arm isLoading=true (synchronously, in the same render that sets the user) when a sign-in is for a user whose athlete row has not been loaded yet, tracked via a loadedAthleteForUserId ref. Token refreshes / repeat events for the same user do not re-arm (no Loading flash). Decision extracted to pure apps/mobile/lib/auth/athlete-load.ts (needsAthleteLoad). The callback stays synchronous (auth processLock hard rule respected).

TESTS: apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/auth/athlete-load.test.ts (pure helper + full state-machine simulation of the sign-in race, pending-athlete path, token refresh, account switch).

VERIFICATION: typecheck all workspaces clean; full suite green (mobile 285, web 39, shared 188); independent agent review APPROVE (no correctness issues). No native module / app.json / metro change, so no expo export gate needed.
close_reason: Implemented + independently reviewed (APPROVE) + quality gate green (typecheck all workspaces, tests mobile 285/web 39/shared 188). Pending commit on branch feat/splash-glow-statement.

title: Mobile match flow: end_match completes match before record_match_result, breaking result + ELO
description:
REPRODUCED via headless two-account harness (Demo Blue vs Demo Red, real RPCs through RLS).

Mobile session match flow: live-step 'End Match' calls end_match (use-live-controls.ts:32) which sets matches.status='completed'. The result step then calls record_match_result, which REQUIRES status='in_progress' and raises invalid_status ('Match is not in progress'). Result: match ends completed with result=null and NO ELO applied (both athletes Δ0). Secondary bug: getCurrentStep maps completed->summary, so a reload skips result/confirm.

Control proof: start->record (no end_match) works: applies ELO (Blue +14 / Red -14), result=submission. The web/challenge flow already uses start->record (never calls end_match), so that's the canonical design.

FIX (mobile-only, no backend migration): handleEnd should stop the local timer, broadcast match-ended to the opponent, and advance to the result step WITHOUT calling end_match. record_match_result then completes the match; the trg_release_session_participants trigger still releases participants on the in_progress->completed transition.

Acceptance: harness scenario A (end-before-record path) must record + apply ELO end-to-end; both athletes confirm; match completes with result=submission and non-zero symmetric ELO delta. typecheck + mobile jest green.
close_reason: Fixed in apps/mobile/lib/match-flow/use-live-controls.ts: handleEnd no longer calls end_match; record_match_result now completes the match + applies ELO. Independently reviewed (APPROVE-WITH-NITS, nits addressed). Verified end-to-end via headless two-account harness across challenge + random matchmaking, submission + draw. Quality gate green: full typecheck + mobile 204 tests.

title: Online presence broken: per-mount channel name breaks Supabase sync
description: apps/mobile/lib/presence/use-online-presence.ts:101 subscribes to 'app:online:${mountId}' (unique topic per mount) while web/test-harness/its own doc use the shared 'app:online' topic. Presence only syncs members of the same topic, so onlineIds only ever contains self and the athlete never appears in web's set. Fix: subscribe to constant 'app:online' with presence key=athleteId; keep mountId only as a stale-write guard, not in the topic name.
acceptance_criteria: Mobile and web share the 'app:online' topic; an athlete online on one platform appears in the other's onlineIds; mountId retained only as stale-write guard.
close_reason: Closed

title: Concierge-seed the launch gym's roster and a live session (cold-start)
description:
PROBLEM: The funnel's ENDPOINT does not exist for a solo new user: the first match depends on a gym manager seeding a live session, and Gyms/Rankings are empty until seeding happens. The strongest, most consistent research finding (atomic-network / gym-by-gym saturation) is that a new athlete must open into a populated LOCAL roster, not a national leaderboard of 6. This is the actual launch-readiness blocker and outranks most client polish for real retention; it is under-weighted because it is ops/data, not code.

EVIDENCE: Recon: 'No real first value is reachable in-app by a new user's own action'; ordinary users cannot create sessions (gym-manager gated, gyms/[id].tsx:175,239); research: saturate ONE gym first, atomic networks (https://uxcam.com/blog/10-apps-with-great-user-onboarding/ ; Andrew Chen atomic network)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Process + data, NOT a schema change. Using the existing gym_managers / is_gym_manager seeding (service-role), onboard the launch gym's full roster and seed at least one live/upcoming session so a new athlete in that city opens into real local opponents and a joinable session. Manually seed the first ~50 athletes via concierge outreach. Add a verified-gym badge as the anti-ghost-town trust signal for the skeptical BJJ audience. This is the precondition that makes the aha reachable; the Home 'Find your first match' CTA and the Gyms tab are dead ends without it.

AFFECTED: jr_be/supabase/ (seed scripts, service-role), no app code change required for the seeding itself

Group: BiggerBet | Effort L | Impact High. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #11).
acceptance_criteria: A test athlete created in the launch city sees a populated local gym roster, not an empty list ; At least one joinable live/upcoming session exists at the launch gym ; The launch gym shows a verified-gym indicator ; The Home 'Find your first match' CTA leads to a real session a user can actually join ; Seeding uses service-role + existing gym_managers infra, no schema migration

title: Instrument the activation funnel end-to-end (analytics layer)
description:
PROBLEM: There is NO product analytics in the repo (only Sentry error tracking). The field-cliff, the aha threshold, and every 'High impact' claim in this roadmap are currently UNMEASURABLE. Pre-launch is the only time to instrument TestFlight cohorts; you cannot retro-measure them. This is the single highest-leverage missing item across all four expert lenses.

EVIDENCE: lib/error-tracking/sentry.ts is the only telemetry; no analytics SDK in package.json; research: the only way to confirm the cliff and define aha is your own funnel analytics (https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/how-to-determine-your-activation ; https://amplitude.com/blog/aha-moment)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Add a lightweight cross-platform analytics module under @jits/shared (so web and mobile share event names) and emit the ladder: signup_started, signup_submitted (with method: email|google), wizard_step_viewed{tos,identity,training}, athlete_activated, push_primer_shown/accepted/declined, first_session_joined, first_match_result (the aha). Choose a privacy-respecting SDK; adding a native analytics SDK may need a new EAS build (verify, flag as build-gated). Wire the activation event off the existing status re-read in use-setup-submit.ts:112-121. Then run a retention-correlation analysis once data exists to confirm/replace the assumed aha.

AFFECTED: packages/shared/src/analytics/ (new), apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/use-setup-submit.ts, apps/mobile/app/(auth)/signup.tsx, apps/web/app/(auth)/ (signup/eua)

Group: BiggerBet | Effort M | Impact High. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #10).
acceptance_criteria: Every funnel event in the ladder fires with correct properties on both platforms (or mobile-first if web is descoped) ; athlete_activated fires exactly once per activation, off the verified status flip ; No PII beyond what privacy policy permits is sent ; A dashboard/query can compute activation rate = signups reaching athlete_activated within the window ; If a native SDK is required, the new-EAS-build dependency is documented

title: Give zero-state Home one Signal-Red primary CTA and branch the free-agent plate copy
description:
PROBLEM: A freshly-activated user lands on an all-empty Home whose single forward action is a low-emphasis mono 'Find a session ->' link inside a dashed box, leaving the brand's one-primary-CTA slot unused for the new-user goal. Worse, the no-session accent plate is rendered UNCONDITIONALLY, so a free agent (who has no gym) is told 'Your gym hasn't designated a live session yet', which is incoherent and signals the app does not know their state. Web already branches this on primary_gym_id; mobile did not.

EVIDENCE: home/index.tsx:176-181 (unconditional 'Your gym hasn't designated a live session' Plate, no primary_gym_id branch); recent-activity-section.tsx (low-emphasis 'Find a session' link); web apps/web/app/(app)/page.tsx:331-333 branches on primary_gym_id; CLAUDE.md one-primary-CTA-per-surface rule

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only UI. (1) When the user has 0 matches and no live session, render ONE full-width Signal-Red primary CtaButton near the top of Home: 'Find your first match' -> routes to /(app)/gyms. This is the surface's single primary CTA; demote the existing buried link to the populated state only. (2) Branch the plate copy on athlete.primary_gym_id exactly like web: gym-having user keeps 'Your gym hasn't scheduled a session yet'; free agent gets 'You're competing as a free agent. Browse partner gyms near you to find an open mat or live session.' Keep the ELO tile narrative as 'Your starting rating'; do NOT turn any numeric value red. Static only, no confetti. CRITICAL: this CTA points at the Gyms tab, so it MUST ship in the same release as the Gyms empty-state fix or it routes users to a dead end.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/(home)/index.tsx, apps/mobile/components/home/recent-activity-section.tsx

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #3).
acceptance_criteria: Zero-state Home shows exactly one Signal-Red primary CTA routing to /(app)/gyms; no second red CTA competes ; The no-session plate copy differs for free agents (no 'your gym' language) vs gym-having users, matching web's branch ; The primary CTA disappears (replaced by the existing populated-state UI) once the athlete has >=1 match, with no flicker during the stats fetch ; No numeric value (ELO, W/L/D) is rendered in Signal Red

title: Reframe the zero-match profile: kill '0%' win rate and anchor the bare ELO 1000 as provisional
description:
PROBLEM: A new jiu-jiteiro sees a '0%' win rate (reads as 'loses every match', not 'new') and a context-free ELO 1000 (1000 of what? good? bad?). In BJJ culture you EARN standing by showing up; branding someone a 0% loser on day one is culturally backwards and de-motivates exactly the competitive user the app wants. The empty/dead-looking profile is the documented #1 first-run risk for a rating app.

EVIDENCE: profile-quick-stats.tsx:62,65 (renders '0%' for null/zero winRate); athlete/competitor-header.tsx:32 (also '0%' when total===0); research: empty profile is the #1 rating-app first-run risk, anchor the number as a starting line (https://uxcam.com/blog/10-apps-with-great-user-onboarding/ ; growth.design/psychology)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only formatting of data already on screen (totalMatches, current_elo). (1) When totalMatches===0 render Win Rate as the word 'New' (NOT '0%', NOT an em-dash which is brand-banned); apply to BOTH profile-quick-stats.tsx AND competitor-header.tsx AND any Home StatOverview so '0' does not leak elsewhere. (2) On the Home EloTile add a small MetaTag 'PROVISIONAL, Unranked until your first ranked match' beneath the 1000. (3) Add one anchoring line near the ELO: '1000 is everyone's starting rating. Win ranked matches to climb.' Keep the ELO number in JetBrains Mono default foreground, NEVER red. Do NOT imply belts map to ELO (belts are earned on the mat).

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/components/profile/profile-quick-stats.tsx, apps/mobile/components/athlete/competitor-header.tsx, apps/mobile/components/ui/elo-system/elo-tile.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/(home)/index.tsx

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact High. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #2).
acceptance_criteria: A zero-match athlete sees 'New' (or equivalent) for win rate, never '0%', on every surface (own profile, competitor header, home stats) ; Home EloTile shows a PROVISIONAL tag and one anchoring sentence when totalMatches===0 ; The ELO numeric value remains JetBrains Mono tabular-nums and is never rendered in Signal Red ; Copy makes no claim that ELO maps to or assigns a belt rank ; Once the athlete has >=1 match, the real win-rate percentage and no PROVISIONAL tag render

title: Gate the cold push prompt behind a branded in-context primer
description:
PROBLEM: The iOS push permission dialog fires automatically the instant the athlete row activates and Home mounts, with zero context. iOS gives exactly ONE native prompt per permission, so a cold ask at the worst possible moment (brand-new user, zero matches, no reason to say yes) buys a PERMANENT per-device deny, after which challenge/match alerts silently never arrive. This is the single highest-confidence fix in the panel: the call site is trivially gateable and expo-notifications is already in the binary.

EVIDENCE: register-push.ts:44-48 (ensurePermission calls Notifications.requestPermissionsAsync cold); push-registration-bootstrap.tsx:23-38 (effect keyed on athleteId fires registration on activation); research: iOS push is opt-in and one-shot (https://www.nngroup.com/articles/permission-requests/ ; https://www.appcues.com/blog/mobile-permission-priming)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Stop auto-firing requestPermissionsAsync on activation. Split registration into (a) push-TOKEN registration that runs when permission is ALREADY granted (getPermissionsAsync === granted, no prompt), and (b) the native prompt, which fires only from the affirmative CTA of a branded primer Plate (dark, sharp corners, no motion). Persist a 'push_primer_shown' flag in AsyncStorage. CRITICAL per critique: do NOT tie the primer to a value moment the cold-start product cannot deliver (first challenge/first session may never happen for TestFlight users). Trigger the primer on a reachable moment: entering the Gyms tab for the first time, or second app open. Copy: 'Get notified the moment someone challenges you or your match is confirmed.' Do NOT add iOS provisional authorization here, that is a build-gated item (see separate BiggerBet).

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/lib/notifications/register-push.ts, apps/mobile/lib/notifications/push-registration-bootstrap.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/gyms/index.tsx, apps/mobile/components/ui/elo-system/ (new primer Plate)

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact High. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #1).
acceptance_criteria: No OS push dialog appears on first Home mount after activation (verified on a fresh device/simulator) ; Push token still registers automatically when permission was already granted, with no prompt ; The branded primer appears once at a reachable trigger (Gyms tab entry or 2nd app open) and only fires the native prompt on its affirmative CTA ; AsyncStorage primer-shown flag prevents the primer reappearing ; Declining the primer leaves the app fully usable and does not re-nag
close_reason: Merged (fix/mobile-first-run, reviewed twice).

title: TestFlight launch crash: monorepo root package.json poisons RN/Hermes ABI (RN 0.82 vs 0.81.4)
description: Root package.json (commit 2538fd9) replaced the workspace scripts+husky with an erroneous, duplicated react-native* dependency block: react-native 0.82.0, react-native-worklets ^0.6.0, react-native-reanimated ^4.1.3, react-native-svg, react-native-web. These hoist to root node_modules and conflict with apps/mobile's SDK 54 pins (RN 0.81.4 / worklets 0.5.1 / reanimated ~4.1.1). npm ls reports react-native 0.81.4 'deduped invalid: 0.82.0'. The mixed RN/Hermes JSI ABI corrupts the Hermes heap at launch. All 4 TestFlight crash logs (builds 2 & 3) are Hermes heap corruption (HadesGC oldGenCollectionWorker tripwire abort, DictPropertyMap::findOrAdd, HiddenClass::findProperty, shared_ptr release) with garbage fault addresses and NO Last Exception Backtrace -- i.e. memory corruption, not an uncaught JS/env exception. Side effects of the same bad edit: root lost scripts (typecheck/test/build:web/db:types) and husky devDep, so the pre-commit gate silently stopped running. apps/mobile/package.json and root package.json both have duplicate keys (botched merge). Fix: restore root package.json to known-good initial version (8d57e85: scripts+husky, no RN deps); dedupe apps/mobile keys; reinstall; verify single RN 0.81.4 tree + expo install --check + expo export.
close_reason: Closed

title: Web in-session challenge accept fails: accepter passed as timekeeper
description: apps/web/hooks/use-session-lobby-realtime.ts:172 calls createInSessionMatch with timekeeperId: currentAthleteId (the accepter, who is also a competitor in the match). Same RPC validation as jits-9l4 rejects this with 'Timekeeper cannot be a competitor in the match'. Result: web user clicks Accept on an incoming challenge and silently sees nothing happen (the broadcast challenge_accepted is never sent because the mutation fails first). The original c0b985e fix was meant to enable the timekeeper-live recorder step on web; that step gates on match.timekeeper_id === athlete.id, so dropping the timekeeper id reverts to fighter-live (no recorder). Two viable fixes: (1) drop the timekeeperId assignment and run the recorder on both fighter devices like mobile does, (2) change the BE RPC to allow caller-as-timekeeper. Option 1 is symmetric with the mobile fix and unblocks the demo without a migration. Affects 013 video flow.
close_reason: Verified fixed on development branch (2026-05-26 audit). jits-zyq + jits-9l4: createInSessionMatch in apps/web/hooks/use-session-lobby-realtime.ts:172 and apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/lobby.tsx:80-82 both omit timekeeperId now (caller is no longer passed as timekeeper). jits-y91: all 4 router.* navigation calls in apps/web/hooks/use-session-lobby-realtime.ts use router.push (lines 86, 110, 122, 176), not router.replace. jits-e0w: apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/confirm-step.tsx wires useMatchCompletion (postgres_changes on matches row) + a myConfirmed && opponentConfirmed effect; auto-advance works for DB-side confirms. jits-65p: both apps/web/app/(app)/match/[id]/results/submission-fields.tsx:70 and apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/submission-fields.tsx:52 label finish_time as '(optional)' correctly.

title: In-session challenge fails: caller-as-timekeeper rejected by RPC
description: Mobile lobby (apps/mobile/app/(app)/session/[id]/lobby.tsx:75) and web realtime hook (apps/web/hooks/use-session-lobby-realtime.ts:172) pass the calling athlete as timekeeperId to createInSessionMatch. The BE RPC create_session_match (jr_be/supabase/migrations/20260501000000_session_matches_ranked.sql:88-92) explicitly rejects timekeeper_id matching either competitor with 'Timekeeper cannot be a competitor in the match' (HINT invalid_timekeeper). Result: every in-session challenge currently fails with a toast and no match is created. Introduced in c0b985e while trying to enable the 013 video flow on web. Mobile recording is per-device (uploaderAthleteId=me.athlete_id in live-step.tsx) and never needed timekeeper to be set, so removing the assignment on mobile is the right fix. Web's fighter-live vs timekeeper-live routing needs a different approach (e.g. recorder always-on for both fighters, or BE RPC change to allow caller-as-timekeeper). Affects the 013 demo.

title: Mobile video upload retry generates new filename; double-orphan path
description: apps/mobile/lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:88-101 retries entire uploadRecording on failure, which calls buildMatchVideoStoragePath again with fresh Date.now() -> NEW filename. First failed upload may leave partial object at path A; retry writes path B; upsertMatchVideo UPDATE points at path B. Two orphan paths possible per session. Fix: pass storage path explicitly to retry, or skip path regeneration.
close_reason: Fixed: storage path built once per recording, reused across retries with x-upsert; compensation deferred to final attempt. Reviewed and approved.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: FIXED (left open for review). Root cause: the retry re-ran uploadRecording, which re-called buildMatchVideoStoragePath with a fresh Date.now(), so attempt 1's partial object stayed at path A while the retry wrote path B (double orphan). Fix: uploadRecording (apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts) accepts an optional storagePath; the hook's handleUpload builds the key ONCE per recording via buildVideoPath and passes the same value to both attempts. With jits-81l's x-upsert the retry overwrites in place. Tests: upload-recording.test.ts 'honors a caller-provided storagePath'; use-video-recorder.test.ts 'retries a failed upload with the SAME storage path' (asserts buildVideoPath called once and both calls share the path).

title: Video upload: orphan storage file when DB insert fails
description: apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts:91-106 and apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts:121-136. Storage PUT succeeds, then upsertMatchVideo throws -> file sits in bucket forever. No supabase.storage.remove() compensation. Web hook surfaces error toast (line 104) but no cleanup. BE has no documented GC. Fix: try { insert } catch { remove storage object }.
close_reason: Complete end to end on the local stack: frontend compensation (final-attempt-only remove() with Sentry observability, jits_web fde6fdb) + backend DELETE policy for the uploader's own path (jr_be ef708c7, verified via live storage-api probe: owner delete 200, opponent delete denied). Prod rollout rides jits-kaf.1.1 (db push blocked on deployment go-ahead).

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: FIXED (left open for review). Root cause: both upload paths wrote the storage object first, then did the match_videos insert with no compensation, so a failed insert stranded the object forever. Fix: in apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts and apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts, when upsertMatchVideo returns not-ok after a successful storage write, the object is removed via supabase.storage.from('match-videos').remove([path]) (best-effort; a failed cleanup never masks the real error), then the failure is surfaced. Tests: apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/video/upload-recording.test.ts ('removes the storage object and throws when the DB upsert fails', 'failed compensation does not mask the DB error') and apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.test.ts ('removes the stored object when the DB upsert fails'). typecheck + full test suite green.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: Frontend half complete and reviewed: best-effort remove() compensation on final attempt only, with observable failure (error OR data.length!==1 reported to Sentry/console). BLOCKED on jr_be: no storage.objects DELETE policy exists for match-videos bucket, so compensation resolves {data:[]} (silent RLS denial) until that migration lands.

title: Mobile video upload uses POST instead of PUT; retry fails with 400
description: apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts:99 uses httpMethod='POST' for Supabase Storage. /object/<bucket>/<path> expects POST for create, PUT for upsert. x-upsert: false + POST works on first try, but retry against same path returns 400 'resource already exists'. The retry-once logic in use-video-recorder.ts:88-101 then double-fails. Web SDK .upload() handles this internally.
close_reason: Complete end to end on the local stack: frontend sends POST + x-upsert:true with the same storage path across retries (jits_web fde6fdb) + backend UPDATE policy with participant check in USING and WITH CHECK (jr_be ef708c7, verified: retry re-PUT 200 for uploader, 403 for opponent). Prod rollout rides jits-kaf.1.1.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: FIXED (left open for review). Root cause: FileSystem.uploadAsync sent POST with x-upsert: false, so a retry against an existing object got 400 'resource already exists'. Fix: apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts now sends x-upsert: true. Kept POST rather than switching to PUT: POST + x-upsert true is exactly what storage-js .upload(path, body, { upsert: true }) sends, and it covers both first-write and overwrite-on-retry, whereas PUT is the update-only endpoint. Combined with jits-voh's stable path, the retry now overwrites the half-written object in place. Test: upload-recording.test.ts 'POSTs to the storage REST endpoint with x-upsert: true'.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: Frontend half complete and reviewed: POST + x-upsert:true (storage-js wire shape), same path reused across retries. BLOCKED on jr_be: overwrite-on-retry needs a storage.objects UPDATE policy for the uploader's own match-videos path; does not exist in any migration yet.

title: Video upload: videoId lost on unmount mid-upload (orphan file)
description: apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts:151-155 and apps/mobile/lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:162-169. Cleanup useEffect only stops media tracks; does NOT cancel in-flight upload promise. State setters fire on unmounted component (React warning + videoId lost). If upsertMatchVideo throws after storage PUT succeeded, file is orphaned in match-videos bucket with no DB row.
close_reason: Fixed: upload+DB chain runs to completion after unmount (mountedRef gates only setState); videoId durable in DB row. Reviewed and approved.

comments.author: Drozes
comments.text: FIXED (left open for review). Root cause: unmount mid-upload fired state setters on an unmounted component, and a DB failure after the storage write left an orphan (no compensation). Fix: both hooks now carry a mountedRef; the storage + DB write chain deliberately runs to completion after unmount (the upsert is NOT gated on mount), only React state setters are skipped. The orphan half is closed by jits-1v6's compensation delete; videoId is durable in the DB row regardless of unmount. Tests: mobile use-video-recorder.test.ts 'completes the upload even when unmounted mid-flight'; web use-video-recorder.test.ts 'finishes the storage + DB write even after unmounting mid-upload'.

title: Matches tab: device QA on real hardware (post-release)
description:
The Matches tab shipped in production OTA be389c6c-e64e-4493-ac33-e54ca9fcf905 (runtime 0.5.0, jits_web main db429e41, 2026-10-06) without the device QA pass; the owner authorized the release without it. Run this checklist on real iOS and Android hardware (include a low-end Android) and file a bead for each failure:
