title: Keep-watching angle switch in the single player: second player, angle 1 plays until angle 2 is in step, crossfade, chip lock (phase 1.5, OTA)
description:
Phase 1.5 of the angle switch work. Builds on jits-xfvd.16 (phase 1, shipped in production OTA ff7e974d). CONTRACT: this bead's DESIGN field and research/2026-10-multi-angle-playback/07-keep-watching-contract.md (untracked in the main checkout; copy it into the branch). The contract wins over this text.
OWNER FEEDBACK 2026-10-06 after testing phase 1 on device: 'When I switch, the video still stalls for a second.' Owner wants angle 1 to keep playing WITH ITS AUDIO until angle 2 is ready, then a crossfade to angle 2; landing later (tap at 11 s, land at 14 to 15 s) is better than a stall; the chips flip at the crossfade. Confirmed: no preload on cellular (angle 2 downloads only after the tap); switcher stays at the top; pill copy 'Syncing angle' / 'Switching angle'.
OWNER DECISION 2026-10-06 (LOCK): once the athlete taps an angle, every chip is locked until the switch lands or is abandoned. No supersede: taps are ignored with no haptic; the tapped chip is busy + selected; every other chip is disabled and dimmed to opacity-disabled 0.5. The engine rejects switchAngle while a switch is in flight. ABANDON always unlocks: sign failure, load error or a hard timeout (8 s Wi-Fi/Ethernet, 12 s cellular and other) tear down the incoming player, keep angle 1 playing (it never stopped), show 'Could not load {label}. Tap it to try again.' and unlock. Background, outside navigation and unmount abandon silently. User seeks and skips stay allowed while pending (they retarget).
SCOPE (summary; details in the contract):
1. A second expo-video player per screen, used only for a switch. Two stacked VideoViews (Android textureView on both). Front and incoming roles swap at the landing; the old front is released (replaceAsync(null)) 300 ms later. At most 2 decoders.
2. Sync: the incoming angle is prepared paused at t0 = map(A.now) + lead*rate. The lead adapts per network class (EWMA of load-to-ready; initial 1.0 s fast, 2.0 s cellular, 3.0 s slow; clamped 0.6 to 5 s). The incoming plays hidden under A, chased into step with the multi-angle sync-controller (read-only reuse), and lands once |error| <= 2 frames for 2 samples. Late-ready retargets are bounded (2) and hidden re-seeks are bounded (3). A cap lands with the residual error (4 s fast, 8 s cellular, 10 s slow). Paused: exact seek, land on the post-seek frame. Covers 0.25x to 2x, user seek/skip/pause/play, A ending, and an angle that does not cover the moment.
3. Audio: A keeps its audio until the crossfade; equal-power 240 ms ramp in 6 steps (kill switch AUDIO_RAMP = cut at the midpoint); approximate angles cut at the bottom of the 80 ms dip.
4. switchState gains mode (keep_watching | in_place), fromSlot, incomingSlot, leadMs. In keep_watching: no held still; activeId and the bottom chrome flip at the landing (= crossfade start); idle and unlock 300 ms later.
5. Quality: incoming signs at quality.currentTarget(); no quality decision while a switch is in flight; a tap during a quality swap runs in_place. Telemetry rebinds to the front player with a playing resync. New fields: switchKeepWatchingCount, switchLeadMs, switchLandedLateMs, switchSyncErrorP95Ms, switchRetargetCount, switchFallbackCount (+ reasons), switchAbandonedCount (+ reasons), switchIgnoredTapCount.
6. in_place fallback (= shipped phase 1): KEEP_WATCHING_ENABLED false, Android decoder-error latch, warm-only device tier, no offsets passed, A not loaded, or a quality swap in flight.
7. Data: nothing before the tap. Per switch about 1.6 MB at 720p / 0.5 MB at 360p (moov + GOP + 5 s buffer), about 0 to 0.5 MB more than phase 1.
PARALLEL SLICES (two worktrees; K1 merges first, K2 rebases):
- K1 Engine owns lib/match-detail/use-video-playback.ts, new lib/match-detail/keep-watching.ts (pure planner and constants), new lib/match-detail/switch-lead-store.ts, lib/video/playback-telemetry.ts, lib/video/use-playback-telemetry.ts, __tests__/support/fake-expo-video.ts (K1 OWNS the fake: two players), and their tests.
- K2 UI owns app/(app)/video/[id].tsx (K2 OWNS the screen), new components/film-room/angle-view-stack.tsx, components/film-room/angle-switcher.tsx (the lock), switch-overlay.tsx (in_place only), syncing-pill.tsx, lib/video/video-status-copy.ts, DESIGN.md registry, __tests__/screens/video-playback.test.tsx (its own inline mock, now two players) and component tests.
- Read-only reuse: lib/video/multi-angle/sync-controller.ts, device-tier.ts, lib/video/quality/network-store.ts, translateAngleTime.
- Then one independent reviewer on the merged diff.
REUSE BY jits-xfvd.3 (phase 2): the owner's cellular 'on demand' standby mode IS this flow; a hot standby is the same machinery with the incoming already in step. keep-watching.ts and switch-lead-store.ts must not import use-video-playback internals; AngleViewStack's z-order, crossfade and dip rules carry over to the multi-angle AngleStack. Telemetry fields are shared.
SERVER TUNING LATER: abandon timeouts become standby.abandonMsFast / abandonMsCellular / abandonMsSlow in get_playback_settings (jr_be-du1.9, client jits-xfvd.17); builtin constants until then.
SHIP: OTA, JS only on runtime 0.5.0 / build 25 (second useVideoPlayer, surfaceType at mount, muted, volume, playbackRate, replaceAsync(null), bufferOptions, expo-device). Rollback: KEEP_WATCHING_ENABLED = false restores phase 1 exactly.
acceptance_criteria:
On an iPhone 12 or newer and a Pixel 6a-class Android, Wi-Fi and LTE-conditioned, 20 switches per cell:
1. No frozen frame over 100 ms from tap to settle while playing (240 fps capture); no black or wrong-moment frame.
2. Audio continuous: no silence over 50 ms across a switch.
3. Tap to crossfade p50 <= 1.5 s Wi-Fi, <= 3 s LTE (switchLatencyMs).
4. Sync at crossfade within 2 frames for exact-synced angles: switchSyncErrorP95Ms <= 67 on Wi-Fi; at most 10% of LTE switches land by cap.
5. Paused: lands paused on the exact moment; Wi-Fi p50 <= 600 ms.
6. Key-moment chips, caption and seek bar flip at the crossfade; the tapped chip is busy from the tap; the pill shows after 200 ms.
7. 0.25x, 0.5x and 2x land in step; seek, skip, pause and play during pending never stall.
8. LOCK: from the tap until idle, chip taps do nothing (no haptic); the engine rejects switchAngle; the tapped chip reads busy + selected and the others disabled and dimmed to 0.5.
9. ABANDON: sign failure, load error and the hard timeout (8 s Wi-Fi / 12 s cellular, tested with a blackholed URL) leave angle 1 playing, show the failure tag once with one announcement, and unlock. Background, navigation and unmount abandon silently.
10. Warm-only Android runs in_place (switchFallbackCount); an Android decoder error latches in_place.
11. No bytes for the other angle before the tap; never more than 2 decoders.
12. One telemetry session per viewing; new fields present; existing fields unchanged.
13. Unit and component tests per contract section 14; full gate green (npm run typecheck, npm run test); independent review clean; OTA shipped; /canvas-sync board 33.

title: Angle switch polish in the single player: seek at swap, held still crossfade, Syncing pill, pressed state (OTA)
description:
Phase 1 of the angle switch work (PM report 2026-10-06). Owner (2026-10-06): 'it flashes a bit and freezes slightly'; wants the button shown as pressed, a crossfade as the new angle loads, and a hovering 'syncing' indicator. OWNER DECISIONS 2026-10-06: ship this phase now as its own OTA; copy 'Syncing angle' (exact) / 'Switching angle' (approximate); NO video preload in phase 1 (pre-sign only); phase 2 preload policy lives on jits-xfvd.3 / jits-xfvd.17.
DIAGNOSIS (use-video-playback.ts on main 335a2335): swapSource (777-832) pauses (819) and replaceAsync's the other URL; no seek is queued so the new item buffers at t=0, reports readyToPlay, and only then markLoaded seeks exactly (517). holdFrame only hides the poster; no image of the outgoing frame is drawn. On screen: frozen frame + silence, likely black on iOS, frame 0 of the other angle, then the target. Estimated about 450 ms on Wi-Fi, about 1 s on 4G (pre-signed). iOS may stall up to 3 s paused (AUTOPLAY_FALLBACK_MS). Analysis per angle refetches (use-video-analysis), so markers and caption shift after the switch.
THE INTERFACE CONTRACT between the two slices is in this bead's DESIGN field and in research/2026-10-multi-angle-playback/06-angle-switch-phase1-contract.md (copy it into the branch). The contract wins over this text.
SCOPE:
1. Seek at replaceAsync settle (not after readyToPlay); re-seek at ready only if more than 0.25 s off.
2. play() at settle when the play intent is on.
3. Held still: generateThumbnailsAsync of the outgoing frame before replaceAsync (cap 150 ms); switchState { phase idle|pending|landing, seq, fromId, targetId, startedAt, approximate, restoring, heldFrame, landedAt, failed } on useVideoPlayback.
4. Precise landing: timeUpdateEventInterval 0.1 during a switch; land within LAND_TOLERANCE_S 0.25 (paused: post-seek first frame, 350 ms fallback); landing to idle after 300 ms.
5. Failure restores the previous angle at the tap moment (no failed panel) with a 4 s tag; supersede rules per contract.
6. SwitchOverlay: still crossfades out over duration.fast (240 ms) on brandOut; approximate angles dip 80 ms each way; cut under Reduce Motion; still dropped after 4 s.
7. SyncingPill: 200 ms show delay, 400 ms minimum, on-media-badge, 2 px sync bar, hidden from screen readers.
8. AngleSwitcher: PressableScale, haptics.select on a new angle, busyId -> accessibilityState busy.
9. useAngleAnalyses prefetch; chrome (caption, seek bar, clock, chips) frozen from a snapshot while pending, swapped at landing.
10. Telemetry: switchLatencyMs redefined as tap to landed; new switchHeldStillCount, switchPillShownCount, switchFailedCount, switchSupersededCount.
11. DESIGN.md Motion registry rows; strings in lib/video/video-status-copy.ts; moment.angleDip = 80 in lib/motion/tokens.ts.
PARALLEL SLICES (two worktrees; B1 merges first, B2 rebases):
- B1 Engine: lib/match-detail/use-video-playback.ts, lib/video/playback-telemetry.ts, lib/video/use-playback-telemetry.ts, their tests, and __tests__/support/fake-expo-video.ts (B1 OWNS the fake; B2 only consumes it).
- B2 UI: app/(app)/video/[id].tsx (B2 OWNS the screen), components/film-room/angle-switcher.tsx, new switch-overlay.tsx and syncing-pill.tsx, new lib/film-room/use-angle-analyses.ts, lib/video/video-status-copy.ts, lib/motion/tokens.ts, DESIGN.md, __tests__/screens/video-playback.test.tsx (own inline expo-video mock) and component tests.
- Then one independent reviewer on the merged diff. Nothing under lib/video/multi-angle or components/film-room/multi-angle changes.
BASELINE: jits-xfvd.14 (phase 0) provides the before numbers; it does not block building.
SHIP: OTA (EAS Update), JS only on runtime 0.5.0 / build 25 (generateThumbnailsAsync, replaceAsync, currentTime, timeUpdateEventInterval, expo-image, reanimated, expo-haptics are all linked). Then /canvas-sync board 33.
acceptance_criteria:
1. On an iPhone 12 or newer and a Pixel 6a-class Android, 20 switches each on Wi-Fi and on LTE (conditioned), playing and paused: ZERO black frames and ZERO wrong-moment (frame 0) frames in 240 fps captures.
2. Wi-Fi pre-signed: p50 tap to landed <= 400 ms, p90 <= 800 ms; LTE p50 <= 800 ms (device telemetry switchLatencyMs).
3. Pressed and selected state on the next frame after the tap, plus the selection haptic.
4. The pill never shows for a switch that lands within 200 ms; always shows for a longer one and stays at least 400 ms.
5. Paused stays paused on the same instant; speed kept.
6. Reduce Motion: cut, static pill, haptic kept.
7. VoiceOver and TalkBack: busy tab state; one announcement at landing, none at start.
8. An injected sign failure returns to the previous angle at the same moment with the failure tag and one announcement.
9. Unit and component tests per contract section 8.
10. Full gate green (npm run typecheck, npm run test), independent review clean, OTA shipped, /canvas-sync redraws board 33.

Next: keep-watching switch (angle 1 keeps playing until angle 2 is ready, crossfade, chips flip at crossfade; landing later than the tap is fine) and LOCK all angle chips from tap until landed or abandoned (timeout/failure). New PM contract in progress.

title: Adaptive playback quality: Auto / High / Data saver, start selection, in-session step down/up on stalls, rendition telemetry (progressive MP4)
description:

Owner decisions 2026-10-05: Auto / High / Data saver per device on Video settings; High = always 720 (no adaptive step-down, hard-failure fallback still applies); Data saver = always 360 (fallback chain); Auto = adaptive; OTA on runtime 0.5.0, JS only.
SCOPE (jits_web owns packages/shared + apps/mobile only; exact file list in spec section 7):
1. Shared pure policy in packages/shared/src/utils/playback-quality.ts: settings types, BUILTIN_PLAYBACK_SETTINGS (identical to jr_be docs/fixtures/playback-settings-defaults.json, mirrored in utils/__fixtures__), parsePlaybackSettings (merge + per-field validation, spec 2.4/2.5), networkKey (spec 2.3), selectStartRendition (spec 3.2, reasons user_high | user_data_saver | network_default | network_unknown | expensive_cellular | expensive_wifi | history_stalls | history_good), pickPlaybackPath, history good/bad rules (spec 3.4).
2. Pure QualityController (packages/shared/src/utils/playback-quality-controller.ts, fake-clock tested): step down on one counted stall >= 1 s (stall_long, fires while open) or 2 stalls within 30 s (stall_repeat); step up after 30 s smooth (90 s after a prior step-down) on wifi/ethernet/4g/5g; cooldowns 2 s down / 15 s up; relapse lock at 360 if a step-down follows a step-up within 60 s; cap 4 switches per screen session, last one reserved for a step-down; guards: not auto, paused, seeking, rate < 1 (2x: stalls count, no step-up), swap in flight, before first frame, rendition unavailable, cap, cooldown.
3. Signer: getMatchVideoPlaybackResult(supabase, id, opts?: number | { rendition, expiresInSeconds }) backward compatible (default 720 = today's behavior); selects playback_360_path + playback_profile; returns target, servedRendition '720'|'360'|'original', available, playbackProfile; sourceKind keeps its file-family meaning. Pinned select test updated; database.ts gains the new columns, client_settings and the two RPCs.

Settings reader getPlaybackSettings (get_playback_settings RPC) + mobile settings store (server this run, else AsyncStorage cache < 30 d, else builtin; never blocks start); preference store (video-playback:quality, default auto); history store (video-playback:history:v1, 8 entries per network key); network store (NetInfo listener, 300 ms start timeout).

title: Player v1: one player per angle, stacked views, audio-bed master clock, opacity swap, swipe switcher, Angles sheet, frame step, switch telemetry (5-device gate)
description:
Report 01 section 6 v1, report 03 section 6.1. All JS on expo-video 3.0.16 (OTA). Builds on the P0 switch fix.
SCOPE:
1. One expo-video player per playable angle (cap 3), each in its own stacked VideoView; the switch is an opacity/z-order swap (hard cut or ~120-150 ms crossfade for hard-synced angles; brief dip for clock-only; cut when Reduce Motion is on). Held last frame, never black.
2. Audio bed = the primary (Best angle) when hard-synced, unmuted, never changes on a switch between audio-synced angles and acts as MASTER CLOCK. Clock-only/unsynced angles play their own audio while visible, with a dip (owner decision).
3. Standby angle kept in step: on each master timeUpdate (0.25 s) compute each slave's expected time in ms; ignore < 1 frame; nudge playbackRate (clamp +-5%) for 1 frame..250 ms; hard re-seek above 250 ms or after seek/stall/rate change/foreground. Trust classes: hard (primary/audio/manual) = hot lock-step; soft (clock) = warm only; none = carry local time.
4. Android 2-decoder cap: at most 2 hot players (visible + 1 standby); a third angle is warm (paused, nudged every 5-10 s, small forward buffer). Decoder errors fall back to warm, then to swap-and-seek. Warm-only on budget Android, in Low Power Mode, and on cellular pre-buffer (owner: slower warm-only switch acceptable on budget Android).
5. Rendition: 720p copy on Wi-Fi; 360p (jr_be-du1.1) on expensive cellular and optionally for standby angles; fall back to normalized_path/original when absent.
6. Default angle = Best angle (server-elected primary, depends on jits-n2im.15) with its tag.
7. Bottom-cluster switcher (44 px targets) + horizontal swipe on the video with page dots; accessibility actions 'Next angle'/'Previous angle'; announce on commit only.
8. 'Approx. sync' tag on clock-only angles, persistent, from sync_source (already in get_match_details).
9. Key-moment chips open on the clearest angle for that moment (jr_be-du1.4 clarity map; fall back to the current angle).
10. Frame step (+-1 frame = 33.3 ms at CFR 30) and slower scrub when paused.
11. Angles sheet listing every expected angle incl. pending and failed (owner decision), per the amended copy deck; quietly add an angle that becomes ready.
12. Match timeline: seek bar, markers and caption use match time (primary clock); an angle not covering the instant is shown unavailable there, never clamped to 0.
13. Switch telemetry on the existing 'Video playback session' event: one session per screen across switches; switchCount, switchLatencyMs (tap to first displayed frame of the target, p50/p90 per session), switchMode (hot | warm | swap), trustClass/syncState, syncResidualMs (p50/p95 from the correction loop), hotPlayers, decoderFallbacks, anglesViewed, renditions; angle extends to mine | opponent | timekeeper and angleCount to 3.
PROTOTYPE GATE FIRST (report 01 'Prototype plan'): behind a debug toggle with an on-screen residual overlay, measure on 5 devices (iPhone 12, iPhone 15/16, Pixel 6a/7a, Galaxy A15/A25, one budget Android): switch latency, residual sync p50/p95 over 10 min, memory, battery per 10 min, thermal, data. Targets: hot switch < 100 ms; residual p95 < 2 frames; battery < 1.5x single angle; no decoder failures with 2 hot angles. Record results in notes; if budget Android fails, ship warm-only there. Measure Android SurfaceView vs TextureView swap.
CROSS-REPO: jr_be-du1.1 (1 s GOP + 360p: needed for warm-switch latency targets and the 360p rendition), jr_be-du1.4 (clarity map for chips), jr_be-du1.3 (shared signed URLs, optional adopt).
SHIP: OTA (EAS Update), JS only on runtime 0.5.0. Anything needing a native module moves to v2 (TestFlight).
acceptance_criteria:
1. 5-device gate results recorded in notes and owner-acknowledged before rollout.
2. Unit tests: correction loop (nudge vs re-seek thresholds), trust-class derivation, match-time mapping incl. uncovered spans, audio-bed selection, decoder-fallback path, telemetry aggregation of switch fields.
3. On device: hard-synced switch lands within 2 frames, audio continuous; clock-only switch dips and plays its own audio with the Approx. sync tag; paused stays paused; speed kept.
4. Angles sheet shows pending/failed angles with copy-deck strings; chips open on the clearest angle.
5. Telemetry shows switchLatencyMs and syncResidualMs from a device session.
6. Full gate green, independent review clean, 3-device on-device review, OTA shipped, /canvas-sync of changed 'Current app' boards.

The multi-angle player's bottom 'thumb zone' angle bar (#53 components/film-room/multi-angle/angle-bar.tsx, design notes proposals/2026-10-05-multi-angle-player item 8) must move to the top before phase 2 ships; the Syncing pill keeps the insets.top + 112 slot under the top switcher in both phases. title: SPIKE: background upload approach for iOS (and Android) compatible with Supabase Storage; decision deliverable
description:
Line refs are at jits_web origin/development 48843b2 (2026-10-04); the local development checkout is ~121 commits behind, so branch the worktree from origin/development. mgr = apps/mobile/lib/video/video-upload-manager.ts, rec = apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts.

Owner decision: background upload ships in THIS release (TestFlight). This spike picks the approach.

FACTS (verified):
- expo 54, expo-file-system ~19.0.22: the new API has no upload; the LEGACY API (expo-file-system/legacy, already imported by rec:1) has createUploadTask(url, fileUri, options, cb) with sessionType defaulting to FileSystemSessionType.BACKGROUND (node_modules build/legacy/FileSystem.d.ts:167, FileSystem.types.d.ts:11,42-45). It sends a WHOLE FILE (binary or multipart); no byte range.
- Current transport is tus-js-client in JS with 6 MiB chunks (Supabase requires exactly 6 MiB). JS does not run while iOS suspends the app, so chaining tus PATCHes in JS cannot continue in the background.
- Not installed: expo-task-manager, expo-background-fetch, expo-background-task. UIBackgroundModes is ['remote-notification'] only (app.json:26-28). runtimeVersion policy appVersion (app.json:13-15), so a native change means a new app version/runtime.
- Supabase Storage supports standard uploads up to 5 GB (signed upload URLs via createSignedUploadUrl + PUT) and tus resumable; our cap is 2 GiB (rec:35-36).

OPTIONS TO EVALUATE:
(A) Hybrid, no custom native code: stay on tus in the foreground; on AppState background, if the remaining bytes are large, abort tus and hand the WHOLE file to createUploadTask(BACKGROUND) as a single PUT to a Supabase signed upload URL (x-upsert true at the same storage path) so iOS nsurlsessiond finishes it while suspended; on return, reconcile (HEAD/list the object, then flip the reserved row to ready). Cost: restarts from byte 0 in the background; double-transfer risk; check signed-URL expiry (2 h) vs long transfers and whether the background session survives app termination by the user (it does not on force-quit).
(B) Pre-slice the file into 6 MiB chunk files and enqueue each tus PATCH as a background upload task: each requires the previous offset to succeed, and completion callbacks need JS -> needs a native module or task-manager wake-ups; likely not reliable without native code.
(C) Small custom Expo native module (Swift URLSession background configuration) that runs the tus PATCH chain natively from URLSession delegate callbacks (iOS wakes the app in the background via handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession), Kotlin WorkManager on Android. Most robust, most work; needs config plugin.
(D) Third-party RN background upload library compatible with Expo SDK 54 (e.g. react-native-background-upload forks): assess maintenance, New Architecture support (jits-vtn notes a TurboModule launch crash history), and tus support.

DELIVERABLE: a decision note in this bead (and research/ doc if long) covering: chosen option, Supabase endpoint and auth (JWT expiry during a long background transfer; signed upload URL avoids it), resume semantics, duplicate/orphan handling with the reserved row (backend JB-C1), Android behaviour, required app.json/plugin changes (UIBackgroundModes 'fetch'/'processing' if used), runtime version bump, and a 1-day prototype result on a physical iPhone: 500 MB upload with the screen locked for 10 minutes. Recommendation going in: (A) for this release if the prototype completes reliably, else (C).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Decision recorded with the prototype result (device, file size, network, locked duration, success/failure, time).
2. JW-B1 description updated with the chosen design, plugin/native changes and runtime version.
3. Open risks listed (force-quit, low power mode, cellular data restrictions).

description: Spec 4.1 (items 1a to 1e). iOS reports 'undetermined' with canAskAgain true after an Allow Once grant lapses on background. 1a readAndReport passes canAskAgain through; not granted + canAskAgain -> explain sheet and re-request, never the denied sheet; denied sheet only when canAskAgain false, and it gains Retry that re-checks getForegroundPermissionsAsync. 1b auto-restore paths (foreground restore, cold start with server live, post-match resume via beforeAutoLive) never attempt the live write after a permission failure; instead a non-blocking toast/CTA (or the explain sheet when active) that re-requests on tap; never auto-pop the system dialog without a tap. 1c use-challenger-arena-reading askedThisSession resets on each foreground and on permission status change. 1d the 60 s live refresh failing for permission while LIVE surfaces the same CTA (once per failure streak); a server-side expiry (looking_for_ranked false on refresh) shows offline in the header chip (spec D7). 1e 30 s timeout on requestForegroundPermissionsAsync; background mid-flow cancels the flow and closes the sheet.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Undetermined+canAskAgain shows explain then the system prompt, never denied. 2) Denied sheet only when canAskAgain false; its Retry re-checks permission and continues when granted. 3) Restore paths with a permission failure make NO live write and show the CTA; the CTA tap runs the interactive flow. 4) No system permission dialog without a user tap. 5) askedThisSession resets on foreground and permission change. 6) Refresh permission failure while live shows the CTA once per streak; server expiry reflected as offline. 7) Permission request times out at 30 s; backgrounding closes the sheet and resolves the flow. 8) Jest covers each branch at the consuming layer.

(7) Housekeeping: e2e runs left invite-e2e-*@example.test accounts in the shared local DB; delete them before any local data export. title: OTA control: verification gate (full gate, config diff, review; no publish without user go)
description:
Verification gate for the OTA update control (no publishing without explicit user go). Depends on the config, controller, UI and docs beads.

STEPS
1. Full gate from repo root: npm run typecheck; npm run test; cd apps/mobile && npx expo export --platform ios --no-bytecode.
2. Native-equivalence: re-run the before/after `npx expo config --type prebuild --json` and `--type public --json` diff (sorted with jq -S) against the commit before this feature with identical env; only extra.updateCriticalIndex (and updateNotice when UPDATE_NOTICE is set) may differ. Also confirm package.json dependency sections are unchanged (only the new "ota:critical" script). This is what makes the change OTA-eligible for runtime 0.3.0.
3. OTA classification per ship-mobile: JS + config extra only => OTA-eligible; record the classification in notes.
4. Optional end-to-end (ONLY with explicit user approval, since it publishes): a Release-config simulator build (npx expo run:ios --configuration Release) pointed at a non-production channel, then eas update to that channel twice: once non-critical (expect banner after background->foreground past the throttle, or after a cold start), once after bumping the counter (expect blocking modal; verify it defers while a match screen is open and appears on exit; Restart reloads into the new bundle). For the test, the throttle may be temporarily lowered locally but must be restored before commit.
5. Independent reviewer (not an implementer) reviews the full diff against the parent spec: brand rules, match guard, no-ops in dev/Expo Go/disabled, no newer native API usage (reloadAsync called with no options), no app.json change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. typecheck, test and expo export all green; outputs summarized in notes.
2. Config diff pasted in notes showing only the extra keys differ.
3. Reviewer sign-off recorded in notes (reviewer is not the implementer).
4. Explicit statement in notes whether step 4 was run (and with user approval) or skipped.
5. No eas update / eas build to production was executed by any agent.
notes: E2E on production (user-approved 2026-09-28). OTA #1 (handler, non-critical) published: group a9bc7f0f-f79b-44f7-a9ff-9ef00a17991d, runtime 0.4.0, commit c45dcab; live manifest verified: prod Supabase ref, updateCriticalIndex 0, no notice.
close_reason: Gate green; 2 independent reviews clean; production E2E: banner verified on-device across OTA groups a9bc7f0f, 188e893a, 1a29d9fa, 6b40a57b, 9287a1e5; critical-modal device check moved to jits-8a59

title: OTA control: soft update banner + critical blocking modal + root mount
description:
Update UI (soft banner + critical modal) and app-wide mount (apps/mobile). Depends on the controller bead (useOtaUpdate API).

FILES
- CREATE apps/mobile/components/updates/update-banner.tsx (presentational: props { onRestart, onDismiss, restarting })
- CREATE apps/mobile/components/updates/critical-update-modal.tsx (presentational: props { visible, notice: string | null, onRestart, restarting })
- CREATE apps/mobile/components/updates/ota-update-bootstrap.tsx (glue: `export function OtaUpdateBootstrap({ suppressed }: { suppressed: boolean })` calls useOtaUpdate and renders banner or modal per prompt). Keep each file under 80 lines.
- MODIFY apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx: render <OtaUpdateBootstrap suppressed={!revealDone} /> ONCE, inside <SafeAreaProvider> right after <Toaster /> (so it is inside ThemeProvider, can read insets/tokens, and sits outside AuthProvider so signed-out users are covered). Do NOT mount it in app/(app)/_layout.tsx and do not mount it per screen.
- CREATE tests: apps/mobile/__tests__/components/updates/update-banner.test.tsx, critical-update-modal.test.tsx.

WHY ROOT: critical fixes must reach signed-out users (login/signup/profile-setup). The match guard is still correct there because useIsInArenaMatch() is a module-level store that reads false when no match screen is mounted. suppressed={!revealDone} keeps the modal from covering the launch splash reveal.

SOFT BANNER (normal update) visual spec, brand rules apply (no shadows, no decorative color, one Signal Red CTA per surface, minimal motion):
- Position: absolute, left 16, right 16, bottom = insets.bottom + 72 (clears the custom EloTabBar in components/layout/elo-tab-bar.tsx; verify on simulator and adjust the constant if it overlaps; export it as a named constant). zIndex high enough to sit above screens, below the RN Modal. pointerEvents box-none on the wrapper so only the banner itself captures touches.
- Container: bg-surface-2 (or bg-card), 1px border-hairline (or border-border), rounded-md (4px), px-3 py-2.5, flex-row items-center gap-3. NO elevation/shadow props.
- Icon: lucide-react-native RefreshCw size 16, color muted token via useThemedTokens().
- Copy: "App updated. Restart for the latest experience." font-body (Inter) text-sm text-foreground, flex-1, max 2 lines.
- Action: <Button variant="outline" size="sm"> "Restart" (NOT the default red variant; the banner must not take the screen's one primary CTA). Disabled + label "Restarting..." while restarting. Avoid the unicode ellipsis if lint forbids; three dots are fine.
- Dismiss: X icon Pressable, hitSlop 8, accessibilityRole "button", accessibilityLabel "Dismiss update notice".
- Motion: none required; if any, a reactive <=100ms opacity fade. No looping animation.
- A11y: announce "App updated. Restart for the latest experience." once via AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility when it appears.
- Hidden (unmounted) whenever prompt !== "banner".

CRITICAL MODAL visual spec:
- React Native <Modal visible transparent={false} animationType="fade" statusBarTranslucent onRequestClose={() => {}} /> (no-op onRequestClose blocks Android back and iOS swipe). Do NOT reuse components/ui/dialog.tsx (its backdrop press closes it). No close button, no backdrop dismiss.
- Full-screen bg-background (opaque) filling the window, content centered, px-6, max-w-md, gap-4. accessibilityViewIsModal on the root View.
- Optional brand touch: <Wordmark size="sm" /> from components/ui/elo-system (static; do NOT use ErMark, it needs animated shared values).
- Heading: "Update ready" in font-heading (DM Sans Bold) text-xl text-foreground.
- Body: notice ?? "You just got an app update with critical improvements. Please restart the app to continue." font-body text-base text-muted-foreground, centered.
- Single CTA: <Button size="lg" className="w-full"> default variant (Signal Red; it is the only CTA on this surface, which satisfies the one-primary rule) label "Restart", "Restarting..." + disabled while restarting.
- If a card is used inside, radius max rounded-lg (8px). No shadows.
- Copy tone welcoming, not alarming: no "error", "warning" or red text besides the CTA.

BEHAVIOR (from controller): "modal" only when a downloaded update is critical and not in a match; "banner" only when non-critical, not dismissed, not in a match; both hidden while suppressed (splash). Restart calls controller.restart().
acceptance_criteria:
1. OtaUpdateBootstrap is mounted exactly once, in apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx inside SafeAreaProvider after <Toaster />, with suppressed={!revealDone}. Not present in app/(app)/_layout.tsx.
2. update-banner.test.tsx: renders the exact copy; Restart press calls onRestart; X press calls onDismiss; restarting => Restart disabled and label "Restarting..."; Restart uses the outline variant (assert no bg-primary class on it).
3. critical-update-modal.test.tsx: renders default copy when notice null and the notice when provided; exactly one button; press calls onRestart; onRequestClose is a no-op (calling the Modal's onRequestClose prop leaves it visible and calls nothing); no dismiss/close control exists.
4. No shadow/elevation props in any new file (grep shadow|elevation returns nothing); radii <= rounded-lg; fonts: heading font-heading, body font-body.
5. iOS simulator check (dev build cannot receive OTAs, so render via a temporary local override or story-style harness, then remove it): banner sits above the tab bar without overlapping it on an iPhone with a home indicator and on a small device (SE); modal covers tabs and bottom sheets; screenshots attached to bead notes.
6. Component files each under 80 lines; npm run typecheck and npm run test green.
notes:

title: OTA control: pure update-policy module + useOtaUpdate hook + jest tests
description:
Update controller: pure policy module + hook + tests (apps/mobile). Depends on the config bead only for the key names below (extra.updateCriticalIndex, extra.updateNotice); can be built in parallel against that contract.

FILES
- CREATE apps/mobile/lib/updates/update-policy.ts  (PURE: no expo/react imports; everything testable)
- CREATE apps/mobile/lib/updates/use-ota-update.ts  (the only file importing expo-updates)
- CREATE apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/updates/update-policy.test.ts
- CREATE apps/mobile/__tests__/lib/updates/use-ota-update.test.tsx

update-policy.ts EXPORTS (names are the contract for the UI bead):
- UPDATE_CHECK_MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 15 * 60_000
- UPDATE_NOTICE_MAX_LENGTH = 280
- readCriticalIndex(extra: unknown): number -> extra.updateCriticalIndex if it is a finite non-negative integer NUMBER; anything else (missing, null, string "3", NaN, -1, 1.5) => 0.
- readUpdateNotice(extra: unknown): string | null -> trimmed string, null if not a string or empty; truncated to UPDATE_NOTICE_MAX_LENGTH.
- extraFromUpdateManifest(manifest: unknown): unknown -> manifest?.extra?.expoClient?.extra (safe on undefined/rollback/malformed).
- isCriticalUpdate(runningIndex: number, updateIndex: number): boolean -> updateIndex > runningIndex (strict).
- shouldCheckForUpdate({ now, lastCheckAt, inFlight, minIntervalMs? }): boolean -> false if inFlight; true if lastCheckAt is null; else now - lastCheckAt >= minIntervalMs.
- isOtaControlEnabled({ isDev, updatesEnabled, isExpoGo }): boolean -> !isDev && updatesEnabled && !isExpoGo.
- type UpdatePrompt = "none" | "banner" | "modal"
- decideUpdatePrompt({ pending, inMatch, suppressed, dismissedUpdateId }): UpdatePrompt, where pending = { updateId: string | null; critical: boolean } | null. Rules in order: pending null => "none"; suppressed (splash still playing) => "none"; inMatch => "none" (deferred, re-evaluated on exit); critical => "modal" (dismissal NEVER hides a critical); pending.updateId !== null && pending.updateId === dismissedUpdateId => "none"; else "banner".

use-ota-update.ts: export function useOtaUpdate(opts: { suppressed: boolean }): { prompt: UpdatePrompt; notice: string | null; restarting: boolean; restart: () => void; dismiss: () => void }
- Enabled = isOtaControlEnabled({ isDev: __DEV__, updatesEnabled: Updates.isEnabled, isExpoGo: Constants.executionEnvironment === ExecutionEnvironment.StoreClient }). Disabled => always prompt "none", never calls any Updates API, registers no AppState listener. useUpdates() may still be called unconditionally (hooks rule); verify it is safe when disabled, else guard.
- Pending update: from useUpdates(): isUpdatePending + downloadedUpdate. If downloadedUpdate.type === NEW: critical = isCriticalUpdate(readCriticalIndex(Constants.expoConfig?.extra), readCriticalIndex(extraFromUpdateManifest(downloadedUpdate.manifest))), notice = readUpdateNotice(same extra) (only surfaced in the modal). If type ROLLBACK: critical false, notice null, updateId null. Never show UI for an available-but-not-downloaded update (reloadAsync needs the downloaded bundle).
- Launch: do NOT call checkForUpdateAsync on mount (native ON_LOAD check already runs; useUpdates reflects its download). Initialize lastCheckAt to mount time so the first foreground within 15 min does not re-check.
- Foreground: AppState listener; when state becomes "active" and the previous state was "background" (ignore "inactive" round trips, matching the project's app:online convention), if shouldCheckForUpdate(...) and !isStartupProcedureRunning: set inFlight, lastCheckAt = now, await Updates.checkForUpdateAsync(); if result.isAvailable await Updates.fetchUpdateAsync(). All errors swallowed silently (no toast; optional Sentry breadcrumb via existing lib/error-tracking/sentry.ts if trivially available). Finally clear inFlight. Checking/fetching is allowed mid-match (background download only); only UI and reload are deferred.
- inMatch = useIsInArenaMatch() from apps/mobile/lib/arena/arena-store.ts (module-level store, works signed-out too, returns false there).
- dismiss(): stores the pending updateId in state (in-memory only; not persisted; a newer update id shows the banner again).
- restart(): no-op if restarting or inMatch; set restarting true; await Updates.reloadAsync() with NO options (reloadScreenOptions may not exist in the field binary's native module; do not rely on newer native APIs). On rejection: restarting false and toast.error("Couldn't restart. Close and reopen the app.") via @/components/ui/toast.
- No new native deps. expo-updates and expo-constants are already dependencies.

TEST CONVENTIONS: jest-expo preset, tests under apps/mobile/__tests__/ mirroring lib paths, @/ alias, renderHook/act from @testing-library/react-native; mock expo-constants like __tests__/lib/env.test.ts (getter on default.expoConfig); use __resetArenaStoreForTests + useArenaMatchScreen from arena-store to drive in-match state (see __tests__/lib/arena/arena-store.test.ts).
acceptance_criteria:
update-policy.test.ts covers at minimum:
1. readCriticalIndex: undefined/null/{}/"3"/NaN/-1/1.5/Infinity => 0; 0 => 0; 7 => 7.
2. readUpdateNotice: non-string => null; "  " => null; "  hi " => "hi"; 300-char string truncated to 280.
3. extraFromUpdateManifest: undefined, {}, {extra:{}}, rollback (undefined manifest), and a well-formed {extra:{expoClient:{extra:{updateCriticalIndex:2}}}}.
4. isCriticalUpdate: 0 vs 0 false; 0 vs 1 true; 2 vs 1 false (older publish never critical); skipped-critical scenario: running 0, critical publish 1 never installed, later normal publish still at 1 => critical true.
5. shouldCheckForUpdate: inFlight blocks; null lastCheckAt allows; exactly minInterval allows; minInterval-1 blocks.
6. isOtaControlEnabled truth table (8 rows).
7. decideUpdatePrompt full matrix incl. critical beats dismissal, inMatch beats critical, suppressed beats all, rollback (updateId null) never matches a dismissal.
use-ota-update.test.tsx (jest.mock("expo-updates"), mock AppState) covers:
8. Disabled (isEnabled false, or __DEV__-equivalent flag, or Expo Go) => prompt "none", checkForUpdateAsync never called, no AppState listener.
9. No check on mount; background->active after 15 min calls check then fetch when isAvailable; before 15 min no call; inactive->active no call; overlapping foregrounds do not double-call (inFlight).
10. check rejects => no throw, no toast, next eligible foreground checks again.
11. downloaded NEW update with higher index => "modal" with notice; equal index => "banner"; dismiss() => "none"; a different updateId later => "banner" again.
12. While a match screen is mounted (useArenaMatchScreen) => "none" for both kinds and restart() does not call reloadAsync; after unmount => prompt returns.
13. restart() calls Updates.reloadAsync once with no args, guards double taps; rejection => restarting false + toast.error.
14. `npm run test -w @jits/mobile` and `npm run typecheck` green.

Deviation: rollback banners are dismissable via a separate in-memory rollbackDismissed flag in the hook (policy contract unchanged: updateId null never matches dismissedUpdateId). reloadAsync called with no args. Sentry breadcrumb omitted (optional).

title: OTA control: criticality counter + app.config.js extra keys (no native change)
description:
Config + criticality counter (apps/mobile). JS/config only; must produce ZERO native-field change.

CONTEXT: apps/mobile/app.config.js already exists and wraps app.json (do NOT convert or touch app.json). It returns {...config, plugins, extra: {...config.extra, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SENTRY_DSN, APP_ENV}}. `eas update` evaluates this file at publish time and embeds the resulting public config in the update manifest at manifest.extra.expoClient; `eas build` embeds it in the binary (read by expo-constants as Constants.expoConfig on an embedded launch). expo-constants 18 returns manifest.extra.expoClient for an update launch and the embedded app.config for an embedded launch, so Constants.expoConfig.extra always describes the RUNNING bundle.

CREATE apps/mobile/update-critical-index.json:
  { "criticalIndex": 0 }
  (Start at 0. Field builds embed no key, which the app reads as 0, so the first handler OTA published at 0 is non-critical, as intended.)

CREATE apps/mobile/scripts/bump-update-critical-index.js (plain Node CJS, no deps): reads the JSON, validates criticalIndex is a non-negative safe integer (exit 1 with a clear message otherwise), writes criticalIndex+1 back with 2-space indent + trailing newline, prints "updateCriticalIndex: N -> N+1". Add npm script in apps/mobile/package.json: "ota:critical": "node scripts/bump-update-critical-index.js". (package.json scripts are not native; still OTA-eligible.)

MODIFY apps/mobile/app.config.js:
  - Read the counter with fs.readFileSync + JSON.parse (path.join(__dirname, "update-critical-index.json")), NOT require (avoid module cache surprises), and validate: missing file => throw with a clear message; non-integer or negative => throw. Failing loudly at publish/build time is intended.
  - Read process.env.UPDATE_NOTICE: trim; empty/whitespace => omit (undefined). No length cap here (the app caps display).
  - Add to the returned extra: updateCriticalIndex: <int>, updateNotice: <string|undefined>. Change NOTHING else (plugins, ios, android, updates, runtimeVersion, version, scheme, etc. must be identical).
  - Add a short comment block explaining the mechanism (monotonic counter, strictly-greater => critical, notice via env so it never persists into later publishes, bump via npm run ota:critical, commit before publishing).

WHY the notice is env-only (not in the JSON): a committed notice would silently ride every later publish; an env var is per-publish.
WHY committed counter (not env): a critical bump must survive into every later publish so a user who skipped the critical one is still forced by the next normal one; env would be forgotten on the next publish.
acceptance_criteria:
1. apps/mobile/update-critical-index.json exists with {"criticalIndex": 0}.
2. `node scripts/bump-update-critical-index.js` (from apps/mobile) increments the value by exactly 1, preserves formatting (2-space JSON + trailing newline), and exits non-zero with a clear message on a missing/invalid file. `npm run ota:critical -w @jits/mobile` works.
3. `npx expo config --type public --json` (apps/mobile) shows extra.updateCriticalIndex === 0 and no updateNotice key; with UPDATE_NOTICE="  Hello  " it shows updateNotice "Hello"; with UPDATE_NOTICE="   " no updateNotice.
4. BEFORE/AFTER native-equivalence proof: with identical env, capture `npx expo config --type prebuild --json` and `--type public --json` on the pre-change tree (git stash or a clean checkout) and after; `diff` of jq -S sorted output shows ONLY the added extra.updateCriticalIndex (and updateNotice when set). Paste the diff output in the bead notes.
5. A corrupt counter (e.g. "abc" or -1) makes `npx expo config` throw a descriptive error.
6. Jest test apps/mobile/__tests__/app-config.test.ts: require("../app.config.js") with a representative { config } fixture (plugins, ios, android, extra.eas, extra.router) and asserts (a) every top-level key except extra and plugins deep-equals the input, (b) extra keeps existing keys and adds updateCriticalIndex equal to the JSON file value, (c) UPDATE_NOTICE trimming/omission, (d) env is restored after each test. Mock fs only if needed; prefer reading the real file.

title: Mobile: in-app OTA update control (soft banner + critical blocking modal)
description:
In-app OTA update control for apps/mobile (mobile only, JS + config extra only, OTA-eligible).

PROBLEM: expo-updates ~29.0.17 (installed 29.0.18) is embedded in the binary but no JS imports it. With runtimeVersion policy appVersion and updates.fallbackToCacheTimeout 0, a published EAS Update downloads in the background on cold start and only applies on the NEXT cold start. Testers routinely run stale bundles, and there is no way to force a critical fix.

SOLUTION (user-approved):
1. Normal update: once an update is DOWNLOADED, show a soft, dismissible bottom banner "App updated. Restart for the latest experience." with a non-red Restart action -> Updates.reloadAsync().
2. Critical update: full-screen blocking modal (no dismiss, Android back blocked), welcoming copy "You just got an app update with critical improvements. Please restart the app to continue.", single Restart button -> Updates.reloadAsync(). Optional per-publish notice text override.
3. Criticality signal: a committed monotonic counter apps/mobile/update-critical-index.json read by the EXISTING apps/mobile/app.config.js into extra.updateCriticalIndex, plus optional extra.updateNotice from env UPDATE_NOTICE. The update manifest carries the publish-time config at manifest.extra.expoClient.extra; the running app compares the downloaded update's index to its own Constants.expoConfig.extra.updateCriticalIndex; strictly greater => critical (monotonic, so a skipped critical is still enforced by a later normal update).
4. Detection: native already checks on launch (checkAutomatically ON_LOAD default). JS adds a throttled check+fetch on every background->active foreground (min 15 min apart). No-op when __DEV__, Updates.isEnabled false, or Expo Go.
5. Match guard: no banner, no modal, no reload while useIsInArenaMatch() is true; show on exit.
6. Release flow: ship-mobile (and testflight-release note) ask "critical?" (default no), bump counter only when critical, optional notice. CLAUDE.md + CHANGELOG updated.
7. Mount once in the ROOT apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx so signed-out users also get critical updates.

KEY DECISION ON CONFIG: apps/mobile/app.config.js ALREADY EXISTS (it wraps app.json: Supabase/Sentry/APP_ENV into extra, conditional Sentry plugin, hard-fail on EAS builds missing Supabase env). There is NO json->js conversion. Lowest risk: add two keys to the extra object that app.config.js already returns. app.json is untouched.

KNOWN LIMITATION: the first OTA carrying this handler applies via the old behavior (next cold start); the feature is effective from the following update. Builds already in the field embed no updateCriticalIndex, read as 0.

Children: config+counter, controller logic+tests, UI+mount, release-flow/docs, verification gate. Full spec is in each child's description/acceptance.

title: No Facebook App ID plumbing exists for the Reels handoff
description:
shareToReels() takes appId as a REQUIRED argument and nothing in the codebase
supplies it. Found by the adversarial review of 0f6ac9f, which grepped and
confirmed: no env var, no constant, no config entry for a Facebook App ID
exists anywhere in apps/mobile or packages/shared.

This is not filed on any existing slice. jits-s6mi.8 covers registering the
Meta app and obtaining the ID; this covers getting that value into the running
app.

## Why it matters more than it looks

Meta requires the App ID for the Reels handoff (and for Stories, since
January 2023). Without it the share fails with a user-facing "The app you
shared from doesn't currently support sharing to Stories"-class error, and
the failure is SILENT from our side: we cannot detect client-side that the
ID was rejected.

The device test (jits-s6mi.6) is the first place a real, possibly-undefined
App ID flows through the module. Note the related one-line fix already in
the current fix round: two guards in index.ts sit OUTSIDE the try block, so
an undefined appId throws a TypeError rather than returning the module's
normal result object. The App ID arriving as string | undefined from config
is exactly the live shape that would hit it.

## Scope

- Decide where it lives. EXPO_PUBLIC_* follows the existing env convention
  (see apps/mobile/lib/env.ts, which reads Constants.expoConfig.extra first
  and falls back to process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_*). It is not a secret: the App
  ID is public by design and ships in the binary either way.
- Add it to .env.example so it is discoverable.
- Surface a clear, early error when it is absent, rather than letting an
  empty string reach the pasteboard and fail opaquely at Instagram.
- Note the bundle ID / package name must ALSO be registered against that App
  ID in the Meta dashboard, or sharing fails with the same undetectable
  error. That half belongs to jits-s6mi.8.

Blocks jits-s6mi.6 (on-device test).
notes: Implemented on feat/hl-p2-core @3a18cfb: EXPO_PUBLIC_FACEBOOK_APP_ID -> app.config.js extra.FACEBOOK_APP_ID -> env.facebookAppId (string|null), not in REQUIRED_ENV. Awaiting review.

title: Meta prerequisites: register a Facebook App ID, take it to Live mode, register the iOS bundle ID and Android package
description:
EXTERNAL PREREQUISITE WITH A LEAD TIME. Nothing in the Reels handoff works without it, and it is
not code, so it can and should start in parallel with Slice B rather than after it.

## WHAT IS REQUIRED

A registered Facebook App ID, in LIVE MODE, with the platform settings filled in. Required for
Sharing to Reels since January 2023.

Live mode requires, per Meta: display name, contact email, PRIVACY POLICY URL, TERMS OF SERVICE
URL, a 1024x1024 icon, app category, app purpose, and the iOS BUNDLE ID and Android PACKAGE
registered under platform settings.

WHAT IT DOES NOT REQUIRE: App Review. Business Verification. Neither applies to a share-only
integration with zero permissions. This is the entire reason the composer handoff was chosen over
the Graph API, where App Review runs 2-8 weeks by practitioner report and Business Verification has
no published turnaround at all.

CHOOSE THE "OTHER" APP TYPE for a share-only app with zero permissions. NOTE: use cases CANNOT BE
REMOVED after app creation, so pick correctly the first time.

## THE CRITICAL-PATH ITEM

The PRIVACY POLICY URL and TERMS URL must be PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE. Today they are not: TERMS.md and
PRIVACY_POLICY.md are repo files served nowhere, and they contain FOUR TBD PLACEHOLDERS
(TERMS.md:64 governing jurisdiction and venue, TERMS.md:68 legal contact email and address,
PRIVACY_POLICY.md:52 rights-request email, PRIVACY_POLICY.md:72 legal contact email and address).
That is tracked as its own issue and blocks this one.

## REGISTER A REAL ONE EVEN IF IT SEEMS OPTIONAL

Whether the Facebook App ID is validated against Meta's registry for the sharing handoff is
GENUINELY UNRESOLVED in both directions, and was investigated. Register a real one regardless: it
is free, it is unreviewed, and the failure mode of a fake or absent ID is a SILENT production break
that cannot be detected client-side.

## UNVERIFIED, WORTH WATCHING

Whether an "Other" type app in Live mode with zero permissions triggers Meta's annual Data Use
Checkup. Meta's own page contradicts itself on this. If it does, it is a recurring compliance task
that needs an owner, not a one-off.

## DELIVERABLE

The App ID, and whatever config surface the client reads it from, wired so that Slice B1 can send
it in the iOS pasteboard payload and the Android intent extra.
acceptance_criteria: A real Facebook App ID exists in LIVE mode under the Other app type, with display name, contact email, public privacy policy URL, public terms URL, 1024x1024 icon, category and purpose filled in, and with the iOS bundle ID and Android package registered under platform settings. The App ID is available to the client for the iOS pasteboard payload and the Android intent extra. Whether the annual Data Use Checkup applies is checked and, if it does, an owner is named.
notes: === 2026-09-27 PM phase 2: OWNER creates the Meta app. Step-by-step: docs/meta-app-setup.md in jr_be branch feat/highlight-reels-alpha (worktree scratchpad/wt/jr_be-int; move/copy to jits_web/docs/meta-app-setup.md when the jits_web branch merges). Use case 'Other', no products/permissions, Live mode with privacy+terms URLs on https://jitsweb.vercel.app (jits-s6mi.7), 1024 icon apps/mobile/assets/icon.png, category Sports, iOS bundle + Android package com.elorated.mobile. The app must and does work without the ID (share-sheet fallback). Hand the App ID to engineering for EXPO_PUBLIC_FACEBOOK_APP_ID in the EAS environments (jits-r71z).

title: Publish TERMS and PRIVACY_POLICY at public URLs and resolve the four TBD placeholders
description:
TERMS.md and PRIVACY_POLICY.md are repo files served at no public URL, and they contain four TBD
placeholders. Both facts block the Facebook App ID going to Live mode, which blocks the Instagram
Reels handoff entirely.

## THE FOUR PLACEHOLDERS

  - TERMS.md:64  governing jurisdiction and venue
  - TERMS.md:68  legal contact email and physical address
  - PRIVACY_POLICY.md:52  the email address for exercising data rights
  - PRIVACY_POLICY.md:72  legal contact email and physical address

Three of the four are "a legal entity's contact details", which is one decision, not three. The
jurisdiction clause is a real legal choice and is the one that needs a lawyer.

## THE HOSTING GAP

Meta's Live mode requires a public privacy policy URL and a public terms URL. Apple already
requires the same for App Store distribution, so this is not Instagram-specific work; it is
overdue work that Instagram happens to surface. Serve both from the marketing/web surface at
stable URLs.

## A SEQUENCING NOTE

jr_be-17f (the consent decision) is likely to REVISE the terms, because TERMS.md:38 currently
grants a licence to host, display and transmit content "within the app, solely as needed to provide
the service", FROM THE UPLOADER ALONE, and publishing athlete B's likeness to a public Instagram
audience is not covered by that under any reading. So expect to publish these, then publish them
again after that decision lands. Publish anyway; the URLs need to exist and be stable, and holding
them hostage to an unresolved legal decision blocks the App ID for no benefit.

## ADJACENT, NOT IN SCOPE HERE

jits-g27 (render waivers.body instead of the hardcoded TOS_TEXT/WAIVER_TEXT constants) is the
related problem that legal copy lives in four places that disagree, and the only one a
non-developer can edit is the one that is never displayed. Fixing that would make future policy
edits cheap. It is not required to publish a URL today.
acceptance_criteria: Both documents are served at stable public URLs. All four TBD placeholders are filled: governing jurisdiction and venue, the legal contact email and physical address (both occurrences), and the data-rights request email. The URLs are recorded in the Meta prerequisites issue.
notes: Pages built on feat/hl-p2-discovery @ 9b8b98c: /terms and /privacy public static routes (apps/web/app/(legal)), TBDs visibly marked, NOT filled (owner input still required before Meta Live mode). Awaiting review; not deployed.

title: Mobile: manual highlight segment picker, render trigger, progress and preview (first caller of the render endpoint)
description:
The first CALLER of the render endpoint, and the reason the endpoint takes [start, end] segments as
input rather than doing its own selection. This ships BEFORE automatic selection, deliberately: it
lets clip quality be evaluated before clip selection is trusted.

## SCOPE

  - On an athlete's own match video, a way to scrub and mark one or more [start, end] segments.
  - Shared-layer mutation to create the video_highlights row with those segments.
  - Progress UI driven by jr_be-15c.6's get_highlight_progress RPC and the realtime status flips.
    Expect roughly 40-70 seconds of wall time plus a possible cold start for something that feels
    to the user like a button press, so this needs a real progress state, not a spinner with no
    end.
  - Preview playback of the finished 9:16 clip.
  - A re-render affordance. NOTE the backend bounds re-renders with a never-reset counter
    (render_total), so the UI must handle "you have hit the re-render ceiling" as a real state
    rather than a generic failure.
  - Terminal failure surfacing: the row carries a scrubbed error_message, and NULL means "no reason
    available", which must render as absence rather than as an error string. Same contract as
    match_videos.error_message in get_video_progress.

## WHAT THIS ISSUE DOES NOT INCLUDE

No share affordance of any kind. Not Reels, not the system share sheet, not save-to-camera-roll.
Preview is in-app playback to a participant, which is the same audience that can already watch the
source. The moment a file leaves the app, jr_be-17f applies and the separate flagged share issue
owns it.

## CONSTRAINTS TO SURFACE IN THE PICKER

Reels accepts 3 to 60 seconds. A clip under 3 seconds is rejected outright. Enforce the bounds in
the picker rather than letting the render succeed and the handoff silently no-op.
acceptance_criteria: An athlete can mark one or more [start, end] segments on their own match video, trigger a render, see real progress driven by get_highlight_progress plus realtime status flips, and preview the finished 9:16 clip in-app. The picker enforces the Reels 3-60 second bounds. Re-render is offered and the render_total ceiling renders as its own explicit state, not a generic failure. A scrubbed error_message is surfaced, and a NULL error_message renders as absence rather than as an error string. NO share affordance of any kind is added by this issue.
notes:
=== 2026-09-27 PM: Highlight Reels Alpha ===
Owner decided generation is AUTOMATIC with feedback + AI regenerate for the alpha (jr_be spec 014). This manual picker is DEFERRED to the fast follow after the alpha (editing research: segment list over the source with expo-video seek-looping preview, one commit render via request_highlight_clip, OTA-eligible, 5-8 dev days). The alpha's player, progress, re-render ceiling and error_message handling are delivered by jits-s6mi.10 and jits-s6mi.9; reuse them here.

title: Highlight Reels phase 2 F6: full-screen highlight/[id] viewer + pre-share sheet (Share to Instagram / Share reel, Save to Photos, Improve this reel), behind highlight_share_enabled
description:
THE ISSUE THAT MUST NOT BE SHIPPED BY ACCIDENT. Read it before wiring any button.

This is the entry point that makes the share path reachable: the button, the sheet, the copy, the
destination picker. It is the ONLY place in either epic where the consent blocker jr_be-17f
actually bites.

## THE RULE

Every outbound share affordance is behind feature_flags key highlight_share_enabled:
  - the Reels handoff
  - the generic system share-sheet fallback
  - save-to-camera-roll

Seeded FALSE. FAIL-CLOSED: a missing flag row means off, following the video_upload_enabled
precedent in jr_be migration 20260918010000. A network failure reading the flag means off, not
"assume on because we already rendered".

THE FLAG MUST NOT BE FLIPPED TRUE WHILE jr_be-17f IS OPEN. jr_be-17f's acceptance criteria now name
this flag explicitly.

Flag-off behaviour is that the affordance is ABSENT, not disabled-looking. A greyed-out "Share to
Instagram" button is a product promise we have not decided we can keep, and it invites someone to
"just enable it for testing" against production data.

## WHAT THE COPY MUST NOT SAY, WHENEVER IT DOES SHIP

The consent flow CANNOT promise revocation. Consent to an Instagram post is irrevocable by
construction, and even the revocable half cannot currently be honoured: there is no delete UI on
either platform, no delete RPC, and status='deleted' is in the CHECK constraint but is never
written (jr_be-umc.4). So the copy can only promise removal from ELO RATED, and it has to say that
at grant time, prominently. Per-clip grant, not blanket. The exact wording is jr_be-17f's output,
not this issue's invention.

## WHY THE RENDER PATH IS NOT BEHIND THIS FLAG

A clip shown only to the two match participants reaches exactly the audience that can already watch
the full source video under participant-scoped RLS. The render path has its own separate kill
switch (highlight_clips_enabled) for operational reasons, not consent ones. Do not conflate the two
flags and do not collapse them into one.
acceptance_criteria: Spec 16.8 F6: every viewer state; Share/Save absent when share disabled (render test, part of guard rule 7); label switches by primaryPath; exactly one red CTA on viewer and in every sheet stage; seen + viewer_opened once per version; improve_tapped; close with/without back stack; Stack.Screen registered; size rules; typecheck + test green; expo export ok. CHANGELOG. Independent reviewer.
notes: Implemented on feat/hl-p2-viewer (507f35a, stubs d387c2c) against spec 16.5/16.6.1 stubs; awaiting independent review + merge after feat/hl-p2-core (delete stubs at merge).

title: Highlight Reels phase 2 F5: lib/highlight-share (capability detection, download-then-handoff, Reels + share-sheet fallback, Save to Photos, clipboard guard, funnel telemetry) + replacement guard test
description:
The Reels handoff must degrade, not fail, and the fallback must be gated exactly as tightly as the
primary path.

## AVAILABILITY DETECTION

Before offering the Reels action, check that Instagram is installed and can receive the intent
(canOpenURL on iOS, package visibility query on Android). This requires the config plugin
declarations to be in place; without them the check returns a confident false on a device where
Instagram is installed.

## FALLBACK

Fall back to the generic system share sheet via expo-sharing, which is ALREADY a dependency
(apps/mobile/package.json). No Meta involvement at all, but it cannot target a specific app, so
Instagram may be buried in the list. That is an acceptable v1 fallback and it is what the research
recommends keeping.

## THE GATE APPLIES TO THE FALLBACK TOO

The generic share sheet is an outbound share to an arbitrary destination. In consent terms it is
identical to the Reels path: it hands the other athlete's likeness outside the two-participant
scope. It sits behind the SAME highlight_share_enabled flag. Do not treat it as the "safe" option
that can ship early.

Same for save-to-camera-roll (expo-media-library is already a dependency). Saving athlete B's
likeness into athlete A's photo library is an outbound share. Same flag.

## INSTRUMENTATION

Instrument the funnel: action offered -> availability check result -> handoff invoked -> app
returned to foreground. The handoff itself gives no success signal (Instagram never tells us
whether the athlete posted), so foreground-return timing plus a lightweight post-return prompt is
the only observability available. Build it now; it is the only way to measure the iOS 16 pasteboard
prompt's drop-off later.
acceptance_criteria: Spec 16.8 F5 in full: capability matrix -> primaryPath; download progress/reuse/timeout/partial delete/sweep; every Reels failure row incl. re-download-once; 3-60 s pre-check; oversize toast; iOS returned-state on AppState active with returned_from_instagram; save permission denied/success/failure; clipboard absent -> press-and-hold, present -> caption_copied; telemetry steps + detail keys; guard test (16.7 rules 1-7) green incl. behavioural gate with shareEnabled false and with prepare -> HIGHLIGHT_SHARE_DISABLED; native-contract suites unchanged and green; admin diagnostics renders; npx expo export --platform ios --no-bytecode ok; typecheck + test green; no dependency/app.json/plugin/metro/babel/eas diff. CHANGELOG. Independent reviewer.
notes: Implemented on feat/hl-p2-core @e2566fb: lib/highlight-share/ + highlight-share-guard.test.ts (contract first block removed), admin diagnostics row, sign-out cache clear. Orchestrator decisions applied: hook logs all share-flow steps incl. share_tapped; no toasts in hook (handoff returns {ok,path,oversize}, saveToPhotos returns SaveOutcome, copyCaption boolean); ShareError has code + retryable. Spec 16.7 item 7 (viewer render test) belongs to F6. Awaiting review.

title: Slice B2: config plugin for LSApplicationQueriesSchemes (iOS) and Android queries package visibility
description:
Both halves of the Reels handoff are invisible to the app without platform declarations, and both
fail SILENTLY when missing, which is the expensive part.

iOS: instagram-reels (and instagram, for the fallback) must be listed in LSApplicationQueriesSchemes
in Info.plist, or canOpenURL returns false and the availability check reports Instagram as not
installed on a device where it is.

Android: the Instagram package must be declared in the <queries> element of AndroidManifest.xml, or
package visibility filtering (Android 11+) hides it from queryIntentActivities and resolveActivity,
with the same consequence.

Both are expressed through an Expo CONFIG PLUGIN, following the existing local-plugin precedent at
apps/mobile/plugins/with-android-backup-rules.js which is already wired into app.json's plugins
array. Do not hand-edit native project files; they are generated.

THIS IS A NATIVE CONFIG CHANGE (app.json plugins), which per the workspace mobile-deploy policy
means TestFlight, not OTA. An OTA cannot carry it and will silently ship without it.
acceptance_criteria: An Expo config plugin (following apps/mobile/plugins/with-android-backup-rules.js) adds instagram-reels and instagram to LSApplicationQueriesSchemes and declares the Instagram package in the Android <queries> element. A prebuild produces both declarations. Availability detection returns TRUE on a physical device with Instagram installed, on both platforms, which is the actual test. No native project files are hand-edited. The change is flagged in the PR as TestFlight-only, not OTA-eligible.

title: Slice B1: custom Expo native module for Meta Sharing-to-Reels (iOS pasteboard + instagram-reels://share, Android ADD_TO_REEL intent)
description:
react-native-share does NOT support Reels. Its targets are INSTAGRAM and INSTAGRAM_STORIES only.
There is no Expo module for this either. A small custom native module is required on both
platforms, and it is the largest single line item in this epic, roughly 3-5 days including expected
iOS pasteboard debugging.

## THE MECHANISM

Meta's documented "Sharing to Reels" integration, opened from alpha to ALL developers in October
2023. It has been open to third parties since F8 in May 2018 and has not changed in eight years
apart from the 2023 App ID requirement, so it is a stable target.

iOS:
  - Write the video to UIPasteboard under the documented backgroundVideo key, along with the
    Facebook App ID. THE backgroundVideo KEY IS DOCUMENTED ON META'S REELS PAGE (unlike the Stories
    page, where it is absent despite the page stating video specs, which is one of the reasons
    Reels was chosen over Stories).
  - Open instagram-reels://share.
  - Use an expiry on the pasteboard item so the payload does not linger.

Android:
  - Build an Intent with action com.instagram.share.ADD_TO_REEL, the content URI, the MIME type and
    the Facebook App ID extra.
  - GRANT URI PERMISSION. The clip is served from a FileProvider content:// URI and Instagram is a
    different app; without FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION (and, for the chooser path, an explicit
    grantUriPermission call) Instagram receives a URI it cannot read and the handoff fails in a way
    that looks like "Instagram ignored us".

## MEDIA CONSTRAINTS TO ENFORCE BEFORE HANDING OFF

3 to 60 seconds. A clip under 3 seconds is REJECTED. 1080p recommended, under 50MB recommended.
Validate client-side and surface a real message rather than letting Instagram silently do nothing;
a silent no-op is the default failure mode of this whole mechanism and is very hard to debug from a
user report.

## THE iOS 16 PASTEBOARD PROMPT

Since iOS 16 the system can prompt before one app reads pasteboard data written by another, and
this handoff works BY pasteboard. A vendor support doc updated 2026-03-31 confirms iOS may prompt
for paste permission and for photo access mid-handoff. Spotify, Strava and Peloton all live with
it, so it is not a blocker, but it sits squarely in the conversion funnel. TEST ON DEVICE EARLY:
this cannot be verified in a simulator, and the frequency and conversion impact of the prompt are
explicitly unverified in the research.

## PREREQUISITE

A registered Facebook App ID in Live mode is required for this to work at all (since January 2023).
See the Meta prerequisites issue. Whether the App ID is validated against Meta's registry is
genuinely unresolved in both directions, so register a real one regardless: it is free, unreviewed,
and the failure mode of a fake one is a silent production break that cannot be detected
client-side.
acceptance_criteria: A custom native module hands a local video file to Instagram Reels on both platforms. iOS writes the documented backgroundVideo pasteboard key plus the Facebook App ID with an expiry and opens instagram-reels://share. Android fires com.instagram.share.ADD_TO_REEL with a FileProvider content URI, the MIME type, the App ID extra AND a read-URI-permission grant. Duration (3-60s) and size are validated client-side with a real user-facing message, never a silent no-op. Verified ON A PHYSICAL DEVICE on both platforms, with the iOS 16 pasteboard prompt observed and its behaviour documented in this issue. react-native-share is NOT used for this path.

title: [epic] Highlight clips (client): manual clip picker, Reels share handoff, Meta prerequisites
description:
Client half of the highlight-clip feature. Backend epic is jr_be-15c; the investigation that
produced both is jr_be/research/instagram-highlight-clips.md (2026-09-23). READ THAT DOCUMENT
BEFORE TOUCHING ANY CHILD ISSUE.

## Product shape

An athlete finishes a match, opens the video, picks (or is offered) a few seconds of it, gets a
9:16 clip back in under a minute, and hands it to Instagram Reels.

## Decisions already made (2026-09-24, owner). Do not reopen.

  - ATHLETE Instagram accounts, not gym accounts. This settles the mechanism as Meta's composer
    handoff rather than the Graph API, permanently.
  - Meta "Sharing to Reels": instagram-reels://share on iOS, com.instagram.share.ADD_TO_REEL on
    Android, with the generic system share sheet as fallback. REELS ONLY for v1, not Stories.
  - react-native-share DOES NOT SUPPORT REELS (its targets are INSTAGRAM and INSTAGRAM_STORIES
    only). A small CUSTOM NATIVE MODULE is required on both platforms. This is the largest single
    line item in the estimate, roughly 3-5 days including expected iOS pasteboard debugging.
  - NATIVE CHANGE, so this ships via TestFlight, NOT OTA. An OTA can never carry a native change;
    it silently ships without it.
  - The render job takes [start, end] segments as input, so manual picking and automatic selection
    are both just callers. Manual picking ships FIRST, deliberately, so clip quality can be judged
    before clip selection is trusted.

## BUILT BUT NOT ENABLED

The share path is gated by jr_be-17f, the consent decision, which is unresolved. Every outbound
share affordance in this epic sits behind feature_flags key highlight_share_enabled, seeded false,
fail-closed (missing row = off), and THAT FLAG MUST NOT BE FLIPPED TRUE WHILE jr_be-17f IS OPEN.

"Outbound share affordance" is broader than Instagram and this matters: the Reels handoff, the
generic system share-sheet fallback, AND save-to-camera-roll all hand the OTHER athlete's likeness
to a destination outside the two-participant scope. All three are behind the same flag. Do not ship
a "just save it to my photos" button as an unflagged convenience; it is the same disclosure.

The RENDER path is NOT gated, because a clip shown only to the two match participants reaches
exactly the audience that can already watch the full source video. See jr_be-17f for the full
reasoning and the one condition it rests on.

## What is impossible, so nobody designs around it

  - PREFILLED CAPTIONS. Instagram stopped honouring third-party captions in August 2015 by explicit
    policy. The industry answer, used by Strava and Peloton, is to render the information into the
    frame.
  - LINK STICKERS / attribution URLs. No programmatic mechanism on either path. An open Meta iOS
    SDK issue requesting attribution-URL support has sat untriaged since March 2025, and Strava
    ships a documented five-tap manual paste ritual instead.

## Explicitly NOT in scope

  - Sharing to Stories (20s video cap; the iOS backgroundVideo pasteboard key is UNDOCUMENTED on
    Meta's Stories page despite the page stating video specs, and react-native-share has unresolved
    reports of it silently failing on iOS).
  - The Graph API content-publishing path.
  - jits-kaf.3, the in-app community feed. Different product surface, not a prerequisite.
acceptance_criteria: An athlete can select segments of their own match video, trigger a render, watch progress, and preview the resulting 9:16 clip. The Reels handoff and the share-sheet fallback are code-complete, on-device verified, and UNREACHABLE behind highlight_share_enabled until jr_be-17f is resolved. The app ships to TestFlight, not OTA. A registered Facebook App ID exists in Live mode with the iOS bundle ID and Android package registered.
