title: Make email confirmation recoverable in-app and build the missing reset-password screen
description:
PROBLEM: If Supabase requires email confirmation, signup hands the user a 'Check your email' wall with only 'Back to Sign In', no resend, no polling, forcing a leave-app/confirm/return/manual-relogin round trip mid-onboarding. Separately, the password-reset loop is BROKEN: the deep link routes the reset token to /login which never consumes it, so a forgotten password is unrecoverable in-app, a hard retention defect independent of FTUE.

EVIDENCE: signup.tsx confirm screen has no resend (verified); auth-context returns needsEmailConfirmation when no session; deep-links/handler.ts:42-44 routes reset-password token to /login with comment 'the dedicated reset-password screen does not exist yet'; auth-context has resetPassword but no resend/updateUser-with-token path

PROPOSED CHANGE: TWO parts, sequenced by a config check FIRST. (A) Check the Supabase project's email-confirmation setting. If it is OFF (cheapest, dominates building resend UI), the entire confirm dead-end disappears at zero engineering cost, but note it is a backend/ops toggle with a spam/throwaway-email tradeoff that pollutes the cold-start roster, so weigh it. If confirmation stays ON, add a 'Resend confirmation email' action (supabase.auth.resend) and prefer the deep-link return path the handler already has over a battery-draining getSession poll. (B) Regardless of the confirmation setting, BUILD the missing reset-password screen: consume the token the handler already forwards and call updateUser with the new password. Part B is the higher-value half and should ship even if confirmation is off.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(auth)/signup.tsx, apps/mobile/lib/auth/auth-context.tsx, apps/mobile/lib/deep-links/handler.ts, apps/mobile/app/(auth)/reset-password.tsx (new)

Group: Medium | Effort M | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #12).
acceptance_criteria: The Supabase email-confirmation setting is checked and the decision (on/off) is documented ; If confirmation is on, the confirm screen offers a working Resend action ; A reset-password screen exists, consumes the deep-link token, and successfully calls updateUser to set a new password ; A user who forgot their password can fully recover in-app without leaving for a browser ; No getSession polling loop runs on a backgrounded screen

title: Remove stubbed/ghost surfaces so the app does not feel broken to a TestFlight reviewer
description:
PROBLEM: A prominent disabled Signal-Red 'Challenge' button on every athlete profile only toasts 'Challenges coming soon', a visible no-op that both violates the one-meaningful-primary-CTA rule and is exactly what the competitor persona says makes them abandon. Settings exposes CHAT and CHALLENGES toggles for features not shipped on mobile, and a realtime-test debug screen ships in the production settings stack.

EVIDENCE: athlete/[id].tsx:124-134 (disabled Challenge button toasts 'Challenges coming soon'); app/(app)/settings/realtime-test.tsx present in shipping settings dir (verified via ls); settings/notifications.tsx exposes CHAT/CHALLENGES toggles

PROPOSED CHANGE: Pure client hides/removals, zero backend, no build. (1) HIDE the head-to-head Challenge button until the flow exists (do NOT repoint it to the in-session-lobby path, that requires an active-session context the profile screen lacks and is M-effort with breakage risk). (2) Hide the CHAT and CHALLENGES settings toggles behind a not-built condition, after verifying they are purely cosmetic and do not orphan backend notification-preference rows. (3) Remove realtime-test.tsx from the production settings stack entirely (move behind a __DEV__ guard rather than dev-flag, so a wrong default cannot ship it).

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(app)/athlete/[id].tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/notifications.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/realtime-test.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/_layout.tsx

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #7).
acceptance_criteria: No disabled 'coming soon' Challenge button is visible on athlete profiles ; CHAT and CHALLENGES toggles are not visible in settings, and hiding them does not break any persisted notification preference the backend expects ; realtime-test is unreachable in a production (non-__DEV__) build ; No Signal-Red CTA in the app is a no-op

title: Make city optional/auto-derived in the activation wizard (the ONLY safe field to slim)
description:
PROBLEM: The wizard hard-blocks submit on a non-empty city even though the backend activation trigger does NOT require it, and the city dropdown is built only from cities that already have gyms with a hardcoded Toronto/Vancouver fallback. So an unserved user is forced to pick a city that isn't theirs and literally cannot complete activation honestly, the field-count cliff made worse by an impossible field.

EVIDENCE: validation.ts:62-69 (isTrainingComplete requires city.trim()); use-setup-data.ts:39-48 (city list gym-derived with Toronto/Vancouver fallback); CLAUDE.md trigger contract needs display_name + current_weight + gym/free_agent + gender + DOB, NOT city; research: every required pre-aha field costs signups (https://foundrycro.com/blog/form-conversion-rate-benchmarks-2026/)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only one-line-plus change that does NOT touch the trigger and never writes guarded columns. Remove city from isTrainingComplete so it is optional for activation, AND auto-derive city from the selected gym's city (the gym join already carries city per CLAUDE.md FK notes) so most users never see a city picker at all. Keep weight + gym-or-free-agent as the activating step (load-bearing for weight-aware ELO). DO NOT defer or remove gender/DOB, the critique verified these are TRIGGER-REQUIRED; removing them would silently break activation (the classic guard/trigger no-op loop) since use-setup-submit.ts:112-121 only shows a generic 'activation failed' with no field-level diagnosis. If free-text city is wanted later, it needs normalization (Toronto/toronto/TO fragments the gym-city dropdown), defer that.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/validation.ts, apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/use-setup-data.ts, apps/mobile/components/profile-setup/training-step.tsx, apps/mobile/lib/profile-setup/use-setup-submit.ts

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact Medium. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #6).
acceptance_criteria: A user can complete activation without manually selecting a city ; When a gym is selected, the athlete's city is auto-populated from the gym's city ; gender and date_of_birth remain required in the wizard gate (NOT deferred) ; Activation still flips pending->active for both gym-affiliated and free-agent users (verified end-to-end) ; No write occurs to any guarded column (id, auth_user_id, current_elo, highest_elo, status, created_at, role)
notes: NUANCE (CHANGELOG 2026-06-02, build 8): city was JUST made a REQUIRED native picker that AUTO-FILLS from the chosen gym. So 'auto-derive from gym' is already shipped; the remaining friction is only the FREE-AGENT case (no gym to derive from). Do NOT blindly revert the required-city decision; scope this to: make city optional ONLY when free_agent, or auto-fill always. ALSO: resolve the gender/DOB activation-requirement conflict (CLAUDE.md says required; bd memory athlete-column-guard-trigger + recon say the trigger does not enforce them) against handle_athlete_activation BEFORE touching anything but city.

title: Add Google SSO to the signup screen
description:
PROBLEM: 'Continue with Google' is the single fastest activation path, it skips three credential fields AND the entire email-confirmation detour, but it lives only on /login. A first-timer who taps 'Register' lands on a credential form and never sees the one-tap option, so the fastest path is invisible to exactly the users who need it.

EVIDENCE: login.tsx:60-64,130-132 (onGooglePress + 'Continue with Google'); auth-context.tsx exposes signInWithGoogle; signup.tsx has zero SSO (grep found no Google/Apple/SSO references); research: SSO lifts signups 20-40%, ~60% of mobile users prefer it (best-practice findings)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Render the existing 'Continue with Google' button as the primary fast path at the TOP of the signup screen, with the email/password form as a secondary 'or sign up with email' section below. signInWithGoogle already exists in auth-context, so this is a pure UI wire-up reusing login's onGooglePress pattern, no new auth code, no build. Adjacent micro-win: add a show/hide toggle to the password fields. HONEST CAVEAT per critique: SSO skips credential entry but the user STILL hits the activation wizard, so do not oversell it as a fast path to a rated profile, only to an account. SEQUENCING RISK: shipping Google without Apple on an iOS launch can INCREASE App Store rejection exposure (guideline 4.8), so do not ship this to the PUBLIC build before the Apple Sign In BiggerBet lands; for the internal TestFlight it is fine.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(auth)/signup.tsx

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact High. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #5).
acceptance_criteria: The signup screen shows 'Continue with Google' as the topmost option with email/password below as a secondary section ; Tapping it invokes the same signInWithGoogle flow as login and lands the user in the activation wizard ; Password fields have a show/hide toggle ; No new native dependency is added and no new EAS build is required ; Account-linking risk is documented as an open question (same email via Google vs email/password)
notes: Apple Sign In (jits-rag) is NOT from-scratch: it was implemented then removed, preserved in commit 844b16d, blocked on the com.apple.developer.applesignin entitlement/provisioning. Re-enable + new build must precede exposing Google-on-signup in the PUBLIC store (guideline 4.8).

title: Turn the 'No Gyms Found' / unserved-city dead-end into a real path (client-only half)
description:
PROBLEM: Every Home CTA funnels to the Gyms tab, whose only empty state is a bare dashed 'No Gyms Found' label with zero call-to-action, and the city filter only lists cities that already have a gym, so a geographically-unserved user cannot even select their own city. This is the single worst FTUE dead-end: an instant uninstall for a competitor in a non-seed city.

EVIDENCE: gyms/index.tsx:213-216 (bare 'No Gyms Found' ListEmptyComponent, no CTA); gyms/index.tsx:91-119 (city set built only from loaded gym cities); CreateGymSheet already imported at gyms/index.tsx:21,159

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only first pass (the backend seeding half is a separate BiggerBet). Replace the bare label with a guided card offering: (1) primary 'Compete as a free agent' action reusing the existing free-agent path (verify the mobile free-agent activation works end-to-end, trigger needs free_agent=true), (2) a secondary 'Request your gym' mailto/support link (ONLY if the mailbox is actually monitored for TestFlight, else omit, an unanswered request churns harder), (3) a 'Show all cities' filter reset so a user is never trapped by an active city filter, and (4) surface the already-imported CreateGymSheet more prominently in the empty state. Do NOT add free-text city here (that is the wizard change, and has data-fragmentation risk).

title: FTUE / first-run activation program (pre-launch)
description:
FTUE / first-run activation program (pre-launch). Full analysis: research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md.

AHA MOMENT: a new user's first recorded RANKED match result that moves their ELO off the bare starting 1000 (the first time a meaningful, earned rating becomes real). NOT 'finished profile', NOT 'saw ELO 1000'.

ACTIVATION MILESTONE (instrumentable): athlete_activated = backend trigger flips pending->active on an athletes UPDATE supplying display_name + current_weight + (primary_gym_id OR free_agent) + gender + date_of_birth (detect at use-setup-submit.ts:112-121).

CURRENT TTV (mobile): ~6 taps / realistically ~10-12 with in-wizard controls, 10 fields, plus an out-of-app email round trip if confirmation is ON. The aha endpoint is currently UNREACHABLE by a solo user (challenge stubbed, sessions gym-manager-gated).

PROGRAM = 3 parallel tracks: (a) make the endpoint reachable (seed a launch gym), (b) make it measurable (instrument the funnel), (c) remove client friction + de-motivators (quick wins). Sequence: Week 0 seed+instrument; Week 1 client-only quick wins (no new build); Week 1-2 config/web; next EAS build for native-gated items. Apple Sign In = jits-rag (4.8 compliance, must precede public Google-on-signup).
design: Respect dark-first Void theme, Signal-Red for CTAs/negative only, numeric data never red, sharp 4px corners, minimal motion, 4 purpose-bound fonts. Do NOT change activation-trigger logic or write guarded athlete columns.
acceptance_criteria: Quick-win client release shipped (no new EAS build); funnel instrumented end-to-end; launch gym seeded with a joinable session; activation rate measurable as a windowed rate.

title: TestFlight launch crash: native TurboModule throws NSException at launch, corrupting Hermes (newArch)
description:
SYMPTOM: ELO RATED iOS TestFlight (com.elorated.mobile) crashes ~0.5s after launch. 4 crash logs (builds 2 & 3) in DoKWRbP0qRetPvPAPA-zLs.xccrashpoint share one signature.

EVIDENCE (crash logs):
- All 4 crash inside Hermes with DIFFERENT garbage fault addrs each run (0x30, 0x08000024, 0x646e6582) and NO Last Exception Backtrace -> heap corruption, not a clean uncaught JS/env throw.
- Decisive frame in 3 of 4: facebook::react::TurboModuleConvertUtils::convertNSExceptionToJSError (RCTTurboModule.mm). Build-2 SIGABRT log: objc_exception_rethrow -> __cxa_rethrow -> std::terminate.
- Throwing call runs on a libdispatch worker thread (ObjCTurboModule::performVoidMethodInvocation) WHILE the JS thread runs the event loop -> off-thread Hermes access -> VM corruption.
- newArchEnabled:true (app.json:12, ios/Podfile.properties.json), Hermes. New-Arch off-thread TurboModule-exception marshalling is the amplifier.

ROOT CAUSE (two layers): (1) a native Obj-C TurboModule method THROWS an NSException during launch [trigger]; (2) RN New-Arch converts it into Hermes off-thread [turns recoverable throw into hard crash]. Must identify WHICH module throws.

TOP SUSPECTS (run unconditionally at launch, native, background queue, depend on signed-build entitlements that differ dev vs TestFlight):
1. expo-secure-store getItemAsync via Supabase auth getSession -- lib/supabase/secure-storage.ts:27 <- lib/auth/auth-context.tsx:57. Keychain entitlement / keychain-access-group mismatch from unfinished eas init / provisioning. NOT try/catch-wrapped at the JS boundary.
2. expo-notifications setNotificationHandler + addNotificationResponseReceivedListener -- lib/notifications/handlers.ts:26,35 <- push-registration-bootstrap.tsx:20 (ungated). aps-environment / remote-notification entitlement (app.json UIBackgroundModes:remote-notification).
Both consistent with the open pre-launch blocker: eas init placeholders + unfinished Apple provisioning (Team ID, push key, entitlements).

RULED OUT: RN/Hermes version skew -- single react-native@0.81.5 tree (npm ls deduped), reanimated 4.1.7 + worklets 0.5.1 correct. Sentry not in the crash stack (initSentry early-returns without DSN; lib/error-tracking/sentry.ts). Supabase module-load env throw (jits-00q) would be a clean JS Error, not this off-thread native corruption.

NEXT STEP (decisive -- get the actual NSException reason):
(a) Release build on-device: npx expo run:ios --configuration Release, read '*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception' in Xcode/Console; OR
(b) Console.app / idevicesyslog filtered to process ELORATED during TestFlight launch; OR
(c) provision EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN + @sentry/react-native expo config plugin so next build reports it.
Then: fix the named module's entitlement/config AND wrap launch-path native calls (SecureStore getItem, notification handler setup) in try/catch so a native throw degrades instead of crashing.

NOTE: This session did NOT change app code (a version-realign attempt was reverted; tree clean, 179 tests green). Crash fix still pending the exception-reason capture above. Related: jits-00q (env-var fix, likely necessary but not sufficient).

title: TestFlight build crashes on launch: Supabase env vars missing from EAS build profiles
description: Cloud EAS builds (preview/production -> TestFlight) crash immediately on app open. Root cause: apps/mobile/lib/supabase/client.ts creates the Supabase client at module load via env.supabaseUrl/env.supabaseAnonKey; apps/mobile/lib/env.ts throws 'Missing env var' when EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY are absent. apps/mobile/eas.json defines only EXPO_PUBLIC_APP_ENV per profile, so cloud builds have no Supabase creds (.env is gitignored, local-only) -> uncaught startup throw -> launch crash. Works in dev because local .env is present. Fix: inject EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY (and EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_*_CLIENT_ID so Google auth works) into all eas.json build profiles; also correct app.json updates.url from PLACEHOLDER_PROJECT_ID to the real EAS projectId.
acceptance_criteria: eas.json development/preview/production profiles include EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID, EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID; app.json updates.url points at real projectId; expo export + typecheck + test green; CHANGELOG updated.
notes:
BUILD #3 SUCCEEDED 2026-05-29 (eas build --profile production --platform ios). EAS log line 6 confirms all 4 EXPO_PUBLIC_ vars (SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY, GOOGLE_IOS/WEB_CLIENT_ID) loaded from production environment and baked into the binary -> launch-crash fix is in the artifact. Build page: expo.dev/accounts/drozes18/projects/elo-rated/builds/7004a400-aca6-4872-9f4a-fb346b0d7cdc ; ipa: expo.dev/artifacts/eas/eQhs3DD6VNboAdsdXQXQRb.ipa . Submitting to App Store Connect/TestFlight now. NOTE: expo-updates is NOT installed (build warned), so app.json updates.url + eas channel are inert until 'npx expo install expo-updates' -- confirms updates.url was never the crash cause. Close after the TestFlight build launches on device without crashing.
ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE (deeper than env-injection, 2026-06-01): builds 3 AND 4 BOTH shipped WITHOUT EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL in the bundle (verified: 0 occurrences in build 4 main.jsbundle) and crashed identically (SIGABRT via ExceptionsManager.reportException rethrow). Prior note's assumption 'loaded from environment = baked into binary' was WRONG. lib/env.ts reads the value via a COMPUTED access processEnv[`EXPO_PUBLIC_${key}`], which babel's EXPO_PUBLIC inliner cannot statically replace -> never inlinable into a release bundle regardless of EAS injection (Google IDs worked because auth-context.tsx reads them via STATIC process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_X). FIX (commit e0e9783): added apps/mobile/app.config.js copying the values into Constants.expoConfig.extra (read first by env.ts, embedded via EXConstants independent of babel inlining) + build-time guard that fails the EAS build if missing. Also consolidated duplicate-named Supabase EAS env vars into single all-env vars (matching working Google vars). VERIFIED: local Release sim build boots + loads live data; build 5 (id 7585e62d-6e43-4118-80ce-c2eafcb78d9b) embeds URL in EXConstants.bundle/app.config (vs 0 in build 4), auto-submitted to TestFlight. Awaiting on-device launch confirmation before close.

title: Web: pending/SSO athletes dead-end at /eua (cannot activate)
description: requireAthlete() redirects every pending athlete to /eua, but /eua only records the waiver and tries 'update athletes set status=active' which the guard_athlete_columns BEFORE-UPDATE trigger silently reverts (NEW.status:=OLD.status for authenticated users). Result: infinite /eua loop with no error ('nothing happens'). Fix: add a profile-completion step for incomplete pending athletes; remove the dead status='active' write from eua-form.
design: Route incomplete pending athletes to a profile-fields form (reuse signup field set: weight/gym-or-free-agent/gender/DOB) that does a real athletes UPDATE -> trigger auto-activates -> then waiver ack. Keep /eua for waiver only.

title: Standby policy client: parse the standby block of get_playback_settings and standbyModeFor() (twin of jr_be-du1.9)
description:
Client half of the multi-angle STANDBY policy. Server half: jr_be jr_be-du1.9 (cross-repo; bd cannot link it). Consumer: jits-xfvd.3 (amended 2026-10-06), which applies the mode per session.
OWNER DECISIONS 2026-10-06: Wi-Fi/Ethernet one hot standby; cellular 4G/5G on demand (no preload); 3G/2G/unknown and Data saver none (on demand, pre-sign only).
SCOPE:
1. Mirror the updated fixture byte for byte at packages/shared/src/utils/__fixtures__/playback-settings-defaults.json; extend BUILTIN_PLAYBACK_SETTINGS and the PlaybackSettings type with the standby block (exact JSON on jr_be-du1.9).
2. parsePlaybackSettings: validate every standby field (modes hot|warm|on_demand; renditions session|360; dataSaver on_demand|warm; maxStandby 0 to 2; warmNudgeMs 2000 to 30000; warmForwardBufferS 2 to 30; booleans); a bad field falls back to its builtin value (spec 05 section 2.5 semantics).
3. Pure helper in packages/shared/src/utils: standbyModeFor({ networkKey, preference: 'auto'|'high'|'data_saver', tier: 'full'|'warm-only', os, settings }) -> { mode: 'hot'|'warm'|'on_demand', rendition: 'session'|'360', maxStandby, playerV1 }. Rules: data_saver -> settings.standby.dataSaver; warm-only tier or (android and !androidHot) caps hot to warm; maxStandby 0 -> on_demand.
4. Unit tests for parse and standbyModeFor (every network key, each preference, both tiers, kill switches).
No player behavior changes here (that is jits-xfvd.3).
SHIP: OTA (JS only), may ride with jits-xfvd.3.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Fixture mirror identical to jr_be (vitest pins it); old cached settings without standby parse to builtin standby.
2. standbyModeFor covers the owner policy table: wifi/ethernet hot, cellular on_demand, 3G/unknown on_demand, data_saver on_demand, warm-only tier never hot, maxStandby 0 on_demand.
3. Full gate green, independent review clean.
notes: 2026-10-06 (PM): also parse standby.abandonMsFast (default 8000), standby.abandonMsCellular (12000), standby.abandonMsSlow (12000), each range 3000 to 30000, for the keep-watching abandon timeout (jits-xfvd.19 contract section 3.1 / owner lock decision). The builtin values must equal ABANDON_TIMEOUT_MS in lib/match-detail/keep-watching.ts.

title: HLS trigger dashboard: Sentry saved queries for the report 02 thresholds (input to jr_be-1qz.19)
description:
Report 02 section 5. Build saved Sentry Discover queries (or one dashboard) on the 'Video playback session' event, filtered surface=match, resumed=false, grouped by video.playback.network (+ cellularGeneration), source, and rendition once Player v1 adds it:
- Startup: p75(timeToFirstFrameMs - signMs); TRIGGER > 2.5 s cellular or > 2.0 s Wi-Fi. Also p75(timeToFirstFrameMs) headline (bead go criterion > 3 s). p75(signMs) > ~700 ms means fix signing/descriptor caching, not HLS.
- Rebuffer: sum(stallMs)/sum(watchMs+stallMs); TRIGGER > 2% cellular or > 1% Wi-Fi, or > 10% of sessions with any stall.
- Abandonment: share of outcome:abandoned_startup (excluding sign_failed, unavailable); TRIGGER > 5% of opens.
- Downgrade: share of cellular sessions on 360p because of stall-downgrade; TRIGGER > 25%.
- Switching (after Player v1): p95 switchLatencyMs; > 500 ms = keyframes/buffering, > 1 s on cellular = HLS low rung likely.
- Volume: monthly delivered bytes > ~2 TB = move delivery to R2 + Worker regardless of HLS.
- Sample-size guard: show session count per bucket; act only with >= 100 sessions per bucket.
Link the saved query URLs in this bead, in jits-n2im.21 notes (satisfies its acceptance 2) and in jr_be-1qz.19 notes. Review monthly until jr_be-1qz.19's revisit date. SHIP: none (Sentry configuration).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Saved queries/dashboard exist with each threshold annotated; URLs in this bead, jits-n2im.21 and jr_be-1qz.19.
2. Verified against at least one real device session.
3. A monthly check is on the calendar/routine until the HLS decision is recorded.
notes: 2026-10-06: adaptive playback quality (jits-xfvd.12, OTA aaa9bb67) added rendition, start_reason, quality_pref, stepdown, network_key, stalled, startup_bucket, rebuffer_bucket and resumed TAGS to the Video playback session event, plus quality extra fields. Full field list and the MP4-vs-HLS reading recipe: jr_be-1qz.19 notes and jits_web research/2026-10-multi-angle-playback/05-adaptive-quality-spec.md section 11. Dashboard queries should filter video.playback.resumed:false (tag) and group by network_key + rendition.

title: iOS capture: fix the H.264 comment, choose codec and resolution explicitly (HEVC vs H.264, 720p vs 1080p)
description:
Line refs are at jits_web origin/development 48843b2 (2026-10-04); the local development checkout is ~121 commits behind, so branch the worktree from origin/development. mgr = apps/mobile/lib/video/video-upload-manager.ts, rec = apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts.

FACTS: rec:23-24 says 'native expo-camera produces MP4 / (H.264/AAC) on both iOS and Android'; prod shows iOS records HEVC (every iOS upload needs the slicer normalize transcode, main.js:663-676). CameraView is videoQuality='720p', no codec, no bitrate (camera-overlay.tsx:134-141); recordAsync passes only maxDuration (use-video-recorder.ts:449). expo-camera 17 supports CameraRecordingOptions.codec ('avc1'|'hvc1'|...) on iOS, and videoBitrate on iOS requires a codec. Reels are upscaled from 720p to 1080x1920 (backend JB-F4).

DECISION (record in notes), recommendation: set codec explicitly to 'hvc1' (keep HEVC: roughly half the upload bytes of H.264, which matters most for upload success; the server transcode is free at our scale per the 2026-09-21 cost note) and move to videoQuality '1080p' ONLY if upload telemetry (JW-A7) shows median upload time stays acceptable; otherwise keep 720p. Fix the comment to describe reality. Android keeps H.264.
These are JS props on an installed native module, so they ship OTA; verify on device that the prop is honoured by the build-23/25 binary before relying on it.
SHIP: OTA (EAS Update) on runtime 0.5.0; JS only, no native change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Comment corrected; codec set explicitly on iOS; unit test asserts the recordAsync options per platform.
2. Device check: ffprobe of a fresh iOS recording shows the chosen codec and resolution (attach output to notes).
3. Decision on 1080p recorded with the telemetry numbers, or deferred with a reason.
notes:
DECISION 2026-10-05 (implementer, feat/video-playback 6d0b2e2): keep iOS capture at HEVC 720p for now; revisit 1080p only with upload telemetry.
Facts: prod evidence shows iOS expo-camera records HEVC (hvc1) at 720p, about 4.7 Mbps (CameraView videoQuality='720p', no codec, no bitrate; AVFoundation picks HEVC on HEVC-capable iPhones). Android records H.264/AAC. Every iOS upload goes through the slicer normalize transcode (H.264/AAC) before broad playback.
Why HEVC: roughly half the upload bytes of H.264 at the same quality, and upload success is the binding constraint (uploads park, background upload is still a spike); the server transcode is free at our scale per the 2026-09-21 cost note.
Why 720p: 1080p would raise bytes about 2.25x at a similar bitrate-per-pixel. Revisit trigger: the upload telemetry from jits-n2im.7 ('Match video uploaded' Sentry events: durationMs, throughputBytesPerSec, bytes, networkType, failedAttempts) shows median upload time acceptable with 4+ weeks of data, and the reel upscale (JB-F4, 720p to 1080x1920) is judged visibly soft. Until then: defer, reason = no upload-time numbers yet.
Done in code: the wrong comment in apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts (claimed H.264/AAC on both platforms) now describes reality.
NOT done (left open on purpose, outside this slice): setting codec='hvc1' explicitly on iOS in recordAsync (use-video-recorder.ts) plus the per-platform recordAsync options unit test (acceptance 1, second half) and the ffprobe device check (acceptance 2). Pinning the codec is a JS prop on the installed expo-camera 17 module (OTA-eligible) but must be verified on a build-25 device first, so it belongs with a device session.
Shipped in production OTA 5df069d4-ab50-49cf-9b7c-a4b54cb625a9 (runtime 0.5.0, main 4d5e490, 2026-10-05) via PRs #47, #48, release #49. Rollback target: 31f5007e-2ba4-4ba6-ab0b-add2aec30c8f. HEVC comment fixed; recordAsync codec pin + device ffprobe pending.

title: Upload: sign-out guard and per-user job scoping; cellular and free-space awareness
description:
Line refs are at jits_web origin/development 48843b2 (2026-10-04); the local development checkout is ~121 commits behind, so branch the worktree from origin/development. mgr = apps/mobile/lib/video/video-upload-manager.ts, rec = apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-recording.ts.

PROBLEM:
- Sign-out (lib/auth/auth-context.tsx:311-355) does not touch the upload manager, persisted jobs or the upload store (resetMatchUploadStore/clearMatchUpload have no callers). An in-flight attempt fails with 'Not signed in' and parks; persisted jobs carry the old uploaderAthleteId and resume when ANY user signs in (bootstrap :49-52), then fail RLS until the 7-day abandon.
- No cellular or free-space checks anywhere (use-network-status.ts exposes connection type, unused by upload code). A 10-min 720p HEVC clip is a few hundred MB; recording can fail on a full disk with a generic error.

WORK:
- Sign-out with active or parked jobs: confirm dialog ('Your match film hasn't finished uploading. Sign out anyway? It will finish next time you sign in as <name>.'). On sign-out, pause runners; jobs resume only for the same athlete id; jobs of another user are never run under a different session.
- Free space: before recording (face-off with recording ON) check free disk (expo-file-system getFreeDiskStorageAsync, legacy) against an estimate for the match length (bitrate x duration x 1.2); warn if short.
- Cellular: upload on cellular by default (owner may change), but show the size on the indicator when on cellular; no wifi-only setting in this release unless the owner asks (open question).

ship-mobile.md changes (OTA path, before the `eas update` step):
- New step "Criticality": AskUserQuestion "Is this update critical (users are blocked by a full-screen Restart prompt until they restart)?" options: No (default, recommended) / Yes. Explain: No => users see a soft dismissible "App updated. Restart" banner once downloaded; Yes => a blocking modal (deferred until they leave any match).
- If Yes: run `npm run ota:critical -w @jits/mobile` (or `cd apps/mobile && npm run ota:critical`), show the before/after index, then commit the bumped apps/mobile/update-critical-index.json (message e.g. "chore(mobile): mark OTA critical (index N)") and push to the release branch BEFORE publishing, so later publishes keep the higher index (a publish from a tree without the bump just loses criticality; it never falsely forces).
- Optionally ask for a notice (only meaningful when critical; default none). If given, prefix the publish command: `UPDATE_NOTICE="..." npx eas update ...`. Never export it into the shell persistently; it must not ride later publishes or builds.
- Verify before publishing: `cd apps/mobile && npx expo config --type public --json | jq '.extra.updateCriticalIndex, .extra.updateNotice'` shows the intended values (with the same UPDATE_NOTICE prefix).
- Report line: include "critical: yes/no (index N)" alongside the update group id.
- Known limitation note: installs whose RUNNING bundle predates the handler (the first handler OTA itself) only get the old behavior (applies on next cold start); from the next publish on the banner/modal work. Builds in the field embed no index and read as 0.
- Add counter edits to the OTA-eligible list: apps/mobile/update-critical-index.json and the extra.updateCriticalIndex/updateNotice keys in app.config.js are JS-config only and OTA-eligible; any OTHER app.config.js change stays TestFlight-required.

testflight-release.md: one short note: a TestFlight build embeds the current updateCriticalIndex (do NOT bump for a build; bump only for a critical OTA) and do not set UPDATE_NOTICE when building.

CLAUDE.md "Mobile deploy: OTA vs TestFlight": add 3 to 5 concise lines: the in-app update control (banner vs blocking modal, mounted once in app/_layout.tsx via OtaUpdateBootstrap, deferred mid-match), the criticality rule (extra.updateCriticalIndex from committed apps/mobile/update-critical-index.json, strictly greater than the running bundle's = critical, monotonic, bump via npm run ota:critical only for critical OTAs, commit before publishing), UPDATE_NOTICE env per publish, and the first-OTA limitation. No em dashes (user rule).

close_reason: Push live on prod 2026-09-28: Vault app.settings.edge_function_url -> /functions/v1/push, read via public.app_setting() (jr_be-g78); push function redeployed.

title: Release checklist: verify the TestFlight build is submitted and installed before publishing an OTA for a new runtimeVersion
description: 2026-09-26: build 22 (v0.3.0) finished on EAS but was never submitted to App Store Connect; testers were on build 21 (v0.2.0) and the 0.3.0 OTA could not reach them. Add an eas submit step (or --auto-submit) and a check that App Store Connect shows the build to the testflight-release / ship-mobile skills.

title: Web: withdraw own pending Arena challenge on entering a session lobby/join wizard (avoid racing Arena push mid-wizard)
description: Re-review M1 of postdemo/web-arena-parity 8a27870: busy gate narrowed to isMatchRoute, so enterMatch / started-join / recover restore run on /session/*/lobby and /join. A challenger whose opponent accepts while they are in the join wizard is pushed into the Arena match; confirm-step.tsx push to lobby or random-match-button push can race it, stranding the Arena opponent. Fix: on entering an immersive non-match route withdraw own pending outgoing (pending-guarded + cancelled broadcast); optionally show a Join toast instead of auto-push. Not a regression vs main.

title: Web accepter rejoin parity: persist accept record so a web accepter who reloads between accept and start rejoins the started match
description: Post-demo review of postdemo/web-arena-parity (06486d2): web has no equivalent of mobile rejoinStartedMatch (AsyncStorage accept record + getStartedChallengesToJoin). If a web accepter reloads between accept and start, acceptedNotEnteredRef is lost and the challenger's 12s fallback leaves the challenger alone in the match. Port with sessionStorage/localStorage, same 10 min window, only-if-never-entered rule.

title: Arena concurrency follow-ups (from 9e77d6a review)
description: F1 accepter whose app dies after accept: challenger's 12s fallback starts the match alone and the accepter has no way back in; remember accepted-not-entered (acceptingRef) and join on opponent-side started UPDATE / foreground / re-SUBSCRIBED. F2 busy-decline of the peer I am entering the match with: store peer id in entryRef, withdraw quietly instead. F3 failed fallback start: re-read once after ~2s and join if started. Minor: toast 'Couldn't start the match with X.' when accepted -> cancelled.
close_reason: Merged 6858eb8 (reviewed twice).

title: Web Arena has no crossing-challenge tie-break (A and B challenge each other)
description: Found in review of fix/arena-challenge-concurrency (9e77d6a). Mobile use-arena-challenge.ts resolves crossing challenges with a lower-challenge-id-is-canonical tie-break so both clients land in ONE match; it also withdraws own outgoing before accepting, declines other fresh pending on entry, and has an accepted-status safety net. Web apps/web/hooks/use-arena-challenge.ts has none of this: a web athlete who accepts while their own challenge to the same person is pending can race into two matches or none, and a mixed web/mobile crossing pair is only protected on the mobile side. Port the accept-time logic (resolveOwnOutgoing + canonical tie-break + entry exclusivity) to web.

title: BE push banners fire on quiet Arena cancels and entry-settle declines
description: Found in review of fix/arena-challenge-concurrency (9e77d6a). The mobile Arena now withdraws or declines challenges automatically: (6b) quiet cancels (crossing-pair other half, stranded own outgoing, accept-failure withdraw of an accepted row) and (6c) the entry-settle decline of every other fresh pending incoming challenge plus the busy-decline of INSERTs that land mid-match. The client treats cancels as quiet (no toast), but any BE notification trigger/push on challenge status changes would still send a banner (e.g. 'X declined your challenge') for these automatic transitions. Check jr_be triggers/edge functions for challenge status notifications and suppress or reword pushes for automatic withdrawals/declines (or tag the write so the trigger can tell). Do not fix in the FE branch.

title: Match video upload follow-ups (from e38ba99 review)
description: 1 keep the screen awake while the match upload is in progress (auto-lock during result/confirm stalls the upload; resumes on foreground); 2 on a failed summary re-fetch schedule one delayed retry (pre-ELO snapshot until next foreground); 3 silent-mode reset on player unmount with two stacked video screens; 4 add video_reslice_limit to GATE_BY_HINT; 5 disabled/not_in_cohort gates retry for 7 days then delete the local clip though copy says it is saved on the device.
notes: PM 2026-10-04: item 1 (keep-awake) -> jits-n2im.1; items 4 (reslice_limit gate) and 5 (7-day silent delete copy) -> jits-n2im.5. Items 2 (summary refetch retry) and 3 (silent-mode reset on stacked players; revisit with jits-n2im.19 expo-video migration) remain here.

title: Push devices never unregistered on sign-out; upsert fails without an UPDATE policy
description: From the first-run hunt: signOut (apps/mobile/lib/auth/auth-context.tsx ~204-213) never deletes the device's push_subscriptions row, so on a shared demo phone A's pushes keep arriving after B signs in. registerPushDevice upserts onConflict athlete_id,token but push_subscriptions has no UPDATE policy (jr_be 20260220000000), so relaunch registration logs register_failed (harmless). Fix: delete this device's token before supabase.auth.signOut(); add an UPDATE policy athlete_id = auth_athlete_id() on the BE. Also: notify_push_function falls back to host.docker.internal unless app.settings.edge_function_url is set on prod (jits-kaf.1.8): pushes likely not sent on prod.

title: Universal links: AASA/assetlinks not served by the web deploy (and /.well-known behind the auth proxy)
description: From the web bug hunt: AASA/assetlinks live in repo-root public/.well-known/, not apps/web/public; apps/web/lib/supabase/proxy.ts matcher covers /.well-known/* (no extension) and it is not in publicPaths, so Apple's unauthenticated fetch would redirect to /login; AASA still has a TEAM_ID placeholder. Also /manifest.webmanifest redirects for logged-out visitors. Fix: move files to apps/web/public/.well-known/, add /.well-known (and manifest) to publicPaths/matcher exclusions, fill the real Team ID (needs the human). Related: jits-d3hb, pre-launch blockers.

title: Web: app:online and lobby:online presence channels never rebuilt after a server close (rate limit)
description: Same dead-channel pattern as jits-fa9x (fixed on mobile). apps/web/hooks/use-online-presence.ts and apps/web/hooks/use-lobby-presence.ts subscribe callbacks handle only SUBSCRIBED. Realtime v2.130 closes a channel past the per-channel presence rate limit (5 calls / 30s, ClientPresenceRateLimitReached); realtime-js drops a closed channel from its registry and never rejoins it, so web presence dies silently until the effect deps change or the page reloads. Web lobby joinLobby/leaveLobby also push into the module channelRef with no dedupe (every toggle is a track/untrack). Additionally the web effects fire-and-forget removeChannel on cleanup, so a remount (display_name/photo change on app:online) can be handed the still-leaving instance by supabase.channel(topic). Lower risk than mobile (a page reload heals it). Fix: port the mobile approach (apps/mobile/lib/arena/use-lobby-presence.ts, apps/mobile/lib/presence/use-online-presence.ts): on CLOSED for the owned channel that is no longer registered, teardown and rebuild on a bounded backoff; skip unchanged track/untrack; await previous removal before rebuilding. packages/shared/src/hooks/use-lobby-sync.ts (web session lobby, hidden route) has the same SUBSCRIBED-only callback but tracks once per join, low risk.

title: Web: realtime challenge INSERT listener prompts while offline (parity with mobile jits-sfry)
description: apps/web/hooks/use-arena-challenge.ts raises the incoming challenge prompt from the realtime INSERT listener without checking that the athlete is live (mobile fixed in jits-sfry, commit 6adcd19 on fix/e14-prompt). Gate it on live state; recovery on go-live should offer it instead.
close_reason: Web already gated (canReceive); regression test added in c38b980.

title: Match detail: the big play placeholder should play, and the match length should read as a length
description: PROBLEM: (1) Each video card is a large 16:9 grey area with a centred play glyph that does nothing when tapped; only the WATCH button below plays. It is the biggest, most obvious tap target on the screen and it is dead. (2) The meta row shows '10:00' next to 'Submission' for a match that ended after a few seconds: that value is the configured clock (matches.duration_seconds), and without a unit it reads as elapsed time. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-48-33-516Z/E17/25-detail_from_Home_Me_scope_.png, E17/29-detail_from_Past_Match_Videos.png. CHANGE: Wrap the poster/placeholder in a Pressable that calls the same onWatch (disabled while processing; accessibilityLabel 'Play <angle label>'); keep WATCH and its testID match-video-watch-<id> (harness tap target). Meta row: render the duration as '10 MIN MATCH' style (e.g. formatVideoDuration + ' clock' or minutes rounded: '10 min round'), mono tabular-nums. Verified NOT a bug: black text on the red WATCH button is the token textOnAccent #0D0F14 (4.60:1 on #E63946; white was 3.54:1 and failed AA), guarded by __tests__/lib/tokens-contrast.test.ts; only the first playable card is Signal Red. FILES: apps/mobile/components/match-detail/match-video-card.tsx, apps/mobile/components/match-detail/match-meta-row.tsx. EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-14, batch D.

title: Home: make the Arena card live-aware
description: PROBLEM: While the athlete is already LIVE (header shows the LIVE pill), Home's 'Find a match' card still says 'Go live in the Arena to challenge athletes...'. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C2/05-Blue_on_the_Home_tab.png. CHANGE: Read isLive from useArenaState() (lib/arena/arena-store.ts, read-only; never mount useArenaLive here) and, when live, show title 'You're live', a LivePill, body 'You're in the lobby. Challenges reach you on any tab.' and CTA 'Open the Arena →'. Offline copy unchanged. Stays the single Signal Red CTA on Home. FILES: apps/mobile/components/dashboard/arena-nudge-card.tsx (+ its dashboard test if one asserts the copy). EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-13, batch C.

title: Dispute form: say what a dispute is for and what happens next
description: PROBLEM: The dispute form says only 'Tell us what happened. A reviewer will follow up.' with a 'Reason (optional)' box. A first-time user does not know whether disputing undoes the result, freezes ELO, or notifies the opponent. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C6/18-Blue_disputes.png (post-submit) and the confirm screen C6/17. CHANGE: Body copy: 'Wrong winner, wrong submission, or it never happened? Tell us. An admin reviews every dispute; ratings stay as recorded until then, and your opponent will see it was disputed.' Placeholder: 'What went wrong? (optional)'. Keep heading text exactly 'Dispute Result' (harness matches /^dispute result$/), testIDs dispute-reason, dispute-submit, dispute-back. The warning glyph moves from stateNegative to amber (disputing is pressure, not a loss); the Submit Dispute button stays the single Signal Red CTA. FILES: apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/dispute-form.tsx. EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-12, batch B.

title: Result + End steps: draw is amber not red, 'Match ended' is not Gain Green, honest end-step copy
description: PROBLEM: (1) Picking DRAW on the result step shows a Signal Red 'loss' plate with a red handshake glyph ('Both athletes lose ELO on a draw'); brand says draws/pressure are amber. (2) The transient End step shows a Gain Green plate and green check for 'MATCH ENDED'; green is reserved for rating increases. (3) Its caption 'RECORDING RESULT...' is not true (nothing is recorded yet; it is an 800ms beat before the Record Result form) and collides with the camera meaning of 'recording'. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/14-Blue_ends_the_match.png; draw case tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-05-52-644Z/C3/17-Blue_records_a_draw.png. CHANGE: Result draw plate -> default plate, amber Handshake (useAmber from components/match-detail/use-amber.ts; for the icon colour use the amber hex matching the class), copy 'Match ends in a draw' / 'Draws cost both athletes rating.' End step: default plate, ink CheckCircle2 (textPrimary), caption 'Up next: record the result'. KEEP testIDs result-record, result-outcome-*, the 'Record result' heading text (harness dismissKeyboard matches /^record result$/). FILES: apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/result-step.tsx, apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/end-step.tsx. EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-11, batch B.

title: Match wizard: name the opponent on the Ready and Live steps
description: PROBLEM: From Ready to End the opponent is never named. The ready panel says 'OPPONENT', the live screen says 'RANKED MATCH' under the clock, and the header is just 'MATCH'. At a demo with several pairs rolling, people want to see who they are on the mat with. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/11-Blue_taps_Ready.png, tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/13-Blue_reaches_the_live_step.png. CHANGE: ReadyPanel label for the opponent shows their display name (numberOfLines 1). KEEP testID 'ready-panel-opponent' by adding an explicit testID prop (today it is derived from label.toLowerCase(), and the harness waits on that id in tools/match-loop/sim/screens.ts waitOpponentReady), and keep accessibilityLabel '<Opponent>, ready|waiting' parsable (harness regex fallback expects 'Opponent, ready'; keep accessibilityLabel prefixed 'Opponent' e.g. 'Opponent <name>, ready' only if the regex is updated too, else keep 'Opponent, ready'). TimerDisplay caption: 'RANKED · VS DEMO RED' (mono caps). Renderer passes opponent.display_name to ReadyStep and LiveStep. Bundle jits-4zp.2 (timer numeral never red; PAUSED and new TIME caption in amber) since it is the same file. FILES: apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/ready-panel.tsx, ready-step.tsx, live-step.tsx, timer-display.tsx, apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-step-renderer.tsx; tests ready-step.test.tsx, live-step-auto-end.test.tsx stay green. EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-10, batch A.

title: Weight step: show what is at stake (Win +N / Draw -N / Loss -N) and stop painting a weight gap red
description: PROBLEM: The weight step is the last calm moment before the roll, and it shows two weights and a red button, nothing about what the match is worth. Also, a division gap is shown on a Signal Red 'loss' plate with a red warning glyph, but a weight gap is not a loss or destructive action. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/09-Blue_lands_on_the_weight_step.png; gap case in tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-32-36-880Z/E12/09-Blue_lands_on_the_weight_step.png. CHANGE: For ranked matches, call the existing typed wrapper getEloStakes(supabase, myElo, oppElo, myWeight, oppWeight) (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:309; the BE RPC calculate_elo_stakes is live, web lobby already uses it) once on mount with a cancelled-ref guard, and render a 3-cell row under the weight tiles: 'WIN +16' (Gain Green number), 'DRAW -8' (amber), 'LOSS -16' (default ink, not red: it is data), all font-mono tabular-nums, label 'At stake' in mono caps. Use the challenger_* fields when the viewer is the challenger else opponent_* (or compute from 'me' as challenger arg; document which). Hide the row on null/error (no spinner, no error UI). Gap plate: switch to default plate + amber Scale icon, copy '<N> weight classes apart. The heavier athlete's rating is adjusted.' The renderer must pass me.current_elo and opponent.current_elo. KEEP testID weight-confirm. FILES: apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/weight-step.tsx, apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-step-renderer.tsx. EFFORT M. RISK low (read-only RPC; failure hides the row). Spec UX-08, batch A.
notes: CORRECTION: colour the LOSS stake with text-negative (state-negative, the AA-tuned red already used for negative deltas on summary and match detail), not default ink. Numbers stay font-mono tabular-nums. So: WIN text-positive, DRAW amber (useAmber), LOSS text-negative.

title: Confirm step: plain-English subtitle and a 'You' panel that is not a spinner before you act
description: PROBLEM: (1) The confirm banner subtitle is 'RANKED. ELO ALREADY APPLIED. DISPUTES ARE REVIEWED BY AN ADMIN.' in 10px mono caps: jargon, shouty, and it does not tell a first-timer what to do. (2) Before the athlete has done anything, the 'YOU' panel shows the same spinner as the opponent's, which reads as 'we are waiting on something' rather than 'your turn'. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/19-Blue_reaches_the_confirm_step.png, tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C6/17-Blue_is_moved_to_the_confirm_step.png. CHANGE: Subtitle (ranked, body font 12px ink-2, sentence case): 'Your rating is already updated. Confirm if this is right, or dispute it and an admin will review.' Casual: 'Confirm if this is right, or dispute it.' ConfirmPanel gets a third state for the viewer before confirming: no spinner, a hairline empty circle and caption 'Your call'; opponent keeps the spinner with caption 'Confirming...'; confirmed keeps the check. Waiting line after confirming: 'Waiting for <opponent name> to confirm...'. KEEP testIDs confirm-verdict, confirm-result, confirm-dispute, confirm-leave and the verdict strings (harness). FILES: apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/confirm-step-panels.tsx, apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/confirm-step.tsx. EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-07, batch B.

title: Arena: fix contradictory lobby copy and the offline 'Looking for Match' title
description: PROBLEM: (1) With nobody online the Arena says 'Nobody has the app open right now. The athletes below are open to challenges and will see it next time they are on.' and directly below 'Not in the app right now, so they cannot answer a live challenge.' Two sentences, opposite promises; and there is nothing to tap on those rows except the profile. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/04-Blue_live_on_the_Arena.png, tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-32-36-880Z/E14/04-Blue_offline_on_the_Arena.png. Note: 'Nobody has the app open' is also false for the viewer, who is live. (2) While OFFLINE the plate is titled 'Looking for Match' (E14/04), which reads like you already are. (3) Sending a challenge gives no tactile feedback. CHANGE: GoLivePlate title: offline 'You're offline', live 'Looking for a match' (body copy unchanged). NobodyOnlineNote: 'Nobody else is live right now. Stay live and anyone who goes live shows up here.' (offline variant: 'Nobody is live right now. Go live and you'll be first in the lobby.'). 'Open to challenges' subtitle: 'Not in the app right now. They can take a challenge once they open it and go live.' Add Haptics.impactAsync(Light) when Challenge is tapped (competitor-row onPress). Do NOT change button accessibility labels 'Go live' / 'Go offline' / 'Challenge <name>' / 'Cancel challenge' or the 'Waiting for <name>' text: the harness taps/reads them. Update __tests__/screens/arena.test.tsx line ~299 (asserts the old note). FILES: apps/mobile/components/arena/go-live-plate.tsx, apps/mobile/components/arena/arena-plates.tsx, apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/arena/index.tsx, apps/mobile/components/arena/competitor-row.tsx, apps/mobile/__tests__/screens/arena.test.tsx. EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-06, batch C.
notes: 2026-09-28: the Arena plates and copy this bead edits are removed by the Mat Board rebuild jits-dq85.15 (spec specs/arena-live-chip/spec.md). Likely supersede once that lands; the haptic-on-Challenge part should carry over.

title: Summary: outcome colours follow the brand (draw amber, no decorative red border) + clearer disputed note
description: PROBLEM: (1) A DRAW summary shows the ELO loss as a Signal Red ▼ 8, but the brand rule is draws/pressure = amber. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C3/22-Blue_reaches_the_summary.png, tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-32-36-880Z/E16/23-Blue_reaches_the_summary.png. The match-detail screen already does this right (components/match-detail/use-amber.ts, match-result-header.tsx deltaClass), so summary and detail disagree. (2) The AFTER rating tile always gets a Signal Red border (EloTile accent -> border-cta), even on a WIN (+16 in green, new rating boxed in red): red used decoratively on a non-CTA. Evidence: C1/22-Blue_reaches_the_summary.png. (3) Disputed note reads 'any rating change stands until then' (fine) but opens with a redundant 'This result was disputed.' under a DISPUTED heading. CHANGE: Draw: verdict text and ▼ delta use useAmber().text, plate variant stays default. Win/loss/disputed unchanged. After-tile border: add an optional tone to EloTile ('positive' | 'negative' | 'amber' | none) and pass positive for a gain, negative for a loss, amber for a draw; never border-cta. Disputed note copy: 'An admin will review it. Your rating change stands until they do.' KEEP verdict strings exactly (YOU WON / YOU LOST / DRAW / DISPUTED / MATCH RECORDED) and the ▲/▼ prefix: the match-loop harness matches them (tools/match-loop/sim/screens.ts VERDICT_RE and readSummary). FILES: apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/summary-step.tsx, apps/mobile/components/ui/elo-system/elo-tile.tsx. BRAND: fixes two violations. EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-05, batch A.

title: Summary: Rematch shortcut that reuses the existing Arena challenge flow
description: PROBLEM: After a match the only exits are Back to Arena and Done; to run it back the athlete must find the opponent in the roster again. At a demo, 'again!' is the most common next action. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/22-Blue_reaches_the_summary.png. CHANGE (no new flow, no new backend): (a) SummaryStep gets optional props opponentId + opponentName (passed by match-step-renderer from opponent.athlete_id / display_name). Render an OUTLINE (secondary, never red) button 'Rematch <first name>' (accessibilityLabel 'Rematch <full name>') that calls router.replace('/arena?rematch=<opponentId>'). Not shown for disputed matches. Keep Back to Arena as the single Signal Red CTA and keep Done (demote it to a text link, keep testID summary-done and text 'Done' because exit-navigation.test.tsx presses it). (b) Arena screen reads useLocalSearchParams().rematch: if that athlete is in Online now, pin their row to the top of the list with a MetaTag 'Rematch' (the row's own existing Challenge button does the work, same sendChallenge, same 3-cap and live rules). If they are not online yet, show a one-line note above Online now: '<Name> isn't back in the Arena yet. Their Challenge button appears here the moment they are.' Clear the param when the athlete challenges or taps away. Do NOT auto-send a challenge. CONTRACT between batches: query param name 'rematch', value = opponent athlete id. BRAND: one red CTA per surface kept. FILES: batch A: apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/summary-step.tsx, apps/mobile/components/match-flow/match-step-renderer.tsx; batch C: apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/arena/index.tsx, apps/mobile/components/arena/arena-plates.tsx, apps/mobile/components/arena/competitor-row.tsx (optional tag). EFFORT M. RISK low-med (touches arena roster ordering; unit-test both states). Spec UX-03.

title: Summary: before/after ELO tiles overflow the screen at 4-digit ratings
description: PROBLEM: With two 4-digit ratings (the normal case: everyone starts at 1000) the before -> after EloTile pair is wider than the content column and bleeds to the screen edges (left tile starts at x~3pt, right tile touches the right edge), while 3-digit results sit inside the margins. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/22-Blue_reaches_the_summary.png and tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-32-36-880Z/E12/21-Blue_reaches_the_summary.png (overflow) vs tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C3/22-Blue_reaches_the_summary.png (fits). Math: size=large is 64px mono; 4 digits ~144pt + px-5 = ~184pt per tile, x2 + arrow + gaps ~409pt vs ~366pt content width on a 402pt iPhone. CHANGE: In the before/after row make each SingleTile flex-1 (drop min-w-[120px] there) and give the number numberOfLines={1} adjustsFontSizeToFit minimumFontScale 0.6, OR use size=medium (44px) in the pair; keep tabular-nums. Must fit 4 digits on a 375pt-wide device (iPhone SE/mini). BRAND: no change. FILES: apps/mobile/components/ui/elo-system/elo-tile.tsx (also used by weight-step and Home; verify those unchanged). EFFORT S. RISK low. Spec UX-02, batch A.

title: Summary: make the 480ms ELO rating tick actually play (plus a closing haptic)
description: PROBLEM: The summary is THE demo moment, but the rating tick does not exist. summary-step.tsx says 'The animated tick (480ms) is handled by EloTile', yet components/ui/elo-system/elo-tile.tsx renders before/after as two static numbers with no animation. Evidence: tools/match-loop/.runs/2026-09-26T03-52-34-503Z/C1/22-Blue_reaches_the_summary.png (1000 -> 1016, static). CHANGE: In EloTile's before/after mode, count the AFTER tile from before to after over exactly 480ms (ease-out, JS requestAnimationFrame or reanimated; integer steps, tabular-nums so width never jitters). Respect AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled (render final value). accessibilityLabel of the ticking Text is always the FINAL value. When the tick lands, fire one Haptics.impactAsync(Light) (success notification on win is also fine). Plays once per mount, never loops. Do NOT animate the ▲/▼ delta text (harness reads summary-elo-delta with /^[▲▼]/). BRAND: the rating tick is the one sanctioned auto-animation (480ms). FILES: apps/mobile/components/ui/elo-system/elo-tile.tsx, apps/mobile/components/match-flow/steps/summary-step.tsx. EFFORT S. RISK low. OTA-safe (expo-haptics and reanimated already in binary). Spec: specs/demo-ux-polish/ux-audit.md UX-01, batch A.

title: Pause re-sync window measured at read arrival, not send time (slow read can flap timer once)
description: From the P0.3 review of 2bcea83: apps/mobile/lib/match-flow/use-pause-resync.ts treats equal-total disagreeing reads as stale only within 3s of lastChangeAt, measured when the read ARRIVES. A reconciler fetch sent before a pause/resume that takes >3s (poor cellular) is applied, flapping the timer until the next 10s poll. Fix: pass each read's send time to subscribeSnapshot listeners; stale iff sent before lastChangeAt; drop the 3s constant. Also nit: use-live-controls MATCH_NOT_PAUSED recovery re-read runs after setBusy(null); keep busy until it finishes.

title: Harden the outbound-footage guard: four confirmed evasions
description:
The unreachability guard has two halves. The Instagram half is solid. The
outbound-footage half has four confirmed evasions, all reproduced by the
reviewer running the parser against adversarial input.

## The evasions

The share-sheet check is a hand-rolled paren parser plus a deny-list of
identifier names. Reproduced:

  Share.share({ message: "Nice one :)", url: videoUri })
    EVADES. The ")" inside the string literal closes the parse early;
    args scanned = '{ message: "Nice one :'. The url is never seen.

  const opts = { url: videoUri }; await Share.share(opts)
    EVADES. Args scanned = "opts". This is the natural refactor the
    moment a payload gets conditional.

  Share.share({ ...payload })
    EVADES.

  Share.share({ url: highlightAsset })
    EVADES. The deny-list is an allowlist by omission:
    renderedClip, assetUri, uri all pass.

The import guard likewise: both
  import * as Sharing from 'expo-sharing'    (single quotes)
  require("expo-sharing")
evade /from "expo-sharing"|from "expo-media-library"|.../

## No live reach today

All four existing Share.share call sites were re-confirmed to pass a URL
and a sentence, never a video file, and nothing imports either package.
These are tripwire weaknesses, not a current breach. Same class as the
original guard gap (which missed apps/mobile/modules/ entirely).

## Why it matters

The legal gate covers the generic share sheet and save-to-camera-roll as
well as Instagram, because all three are the same disclosure of the other
athlete's likeness outside the participant set. The guard is what stops
someone shipping "just save it to my photos" as an unflagged convenience.
A tripwire that a routine refactor walks past is not a tripwire.

## Recommended shape

1. Drop the parser. Flag any scanned file containing `Share.share` AND a
   video identifier ANYWHERE in the file. Coarser, some false positives,
   but it cannot be walked past by a refactor or a stray paren, and it
   matches how the Instagram half already works.
2. Import guard -> /["']expo-sharing["']|["']expo-media-library["']/
   which covers single quotes, require() and dynamic import() at once.
3. toHaveLength(4) is a fine anti-vacuity anchor, but a bare count invites
   a silent bump when a legitimate profile-share button lands. Assert the
   SET of four relative paths instead, so a reviewer must look at which
   file changed. Keep the tripwire either way: a new share button
   deserving a deliberate look is a feature, not a cost.

Must land before the share entry point does.

title: Slice B5: TestFlight build for the Reels native module, plus on-device pasteboard-prompt and drop-off measurement
description:
The Reels module and its config plugin are NATIVE changes: a new native module, plus app.json plugin config touching Info.plist and AndroidManifest. Per the workspace mobile-deploy policy this ships via TestFlight (eas build), NOT via EAS Update. An OTA can never carry a native change and will silently ship without it, which here means the share action exists in JS and the platform declarations do not, so availability detection returns a confident false on a device where Instagram is installed. That is exactly the silent failure this policy exists to prevent.

On the build, measure what cannot be measured any other way: how often the iOS 16 pasteboard prompt appears, whether the photo-access prompt appears mid-handoff, and where athletes drop out of the funnel instrumented in Slice B3. Frequency and conversion impact of that prompt are explicitly listed as unverified in research section 9, so this is the issue that verifies them.

Worth a direct look on the same pass: JudoFlow (App Store v1.1.2, ~2026-09-11) advertises 'your training becomes a swipeable story ... ready to share to your Instagram story'. Mechanism undisclosed. It is the nearest live implementation of this feature in a grappling app.
acceptance_criteria: A TestFlight build carrying the native module and the config plugin is in testers' hands. The iOS pasteboard prompt's actual frequency and the funnel drop-off are recorded in this issue as numbers, not impressions. The share affordance remains flag-off in that build.
notes: === 2026-09-27 PM phase 2 (spec 16.9): RECON FACTS: the InstagramReels module (0f6ac9f, autolinked from ./modules) and with-instagram-reels plugin are in build 22 (v0.3.0, submitted 2026-09-26, submission bef613fa; EAS build id/commit unrecorded) and build 23 (v0.4.0, EAS c430db44-d805-4ce3-aede-b7baf00c7959 from 523daa8; auto-submit d6cb1244 UNCONFIRMED, jits-1c5i). expo-sharing, expo-media-library(+plugin), expo-file-system, expo-video are in builds 21-23. expo-clipboard is NOT installed. So the phase-2 funnel ships TIER 1 as an OTA to runtime 0.4.0 (no build needed) and this bead becomes TIER 2: (1) add expo-clipboard + marketing version bump 0.4.0 -> 0.5.0 + TestFlight build via testflight-release, SUBMITTED and confirmed with eas build:view before any OTA targets 0.5.0; (2) optional device-verified spike: Reels module iOS captionText as public.utf8-plain-text on the same pasteboard item (ship only if Instagram still accepts the payload; native-contract tests extended); (3) the original on-device measurements: iOS 16+ Allow Paste prompt frequency/outcome, Instagram photo-access prompt, returned_from_instagram timing, Reels vs share-sheet mix, recorded as numbers. BEFORE the tier-1 OTA, confirm the five items in spec 16.9 (build 23 Ready to Test; admin diagnostics 'Reels module: present' on an internal device after OTA; LSApplicationQueriesSchemes instagram-reels + NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription in build 23; production channel mapping; EXPO_PUBLIC_FACEBOOK_APP_ID in the EAS environment once the Meta app exists).

title: match_videos.duration_seconds is never sent on upload
description:
Verified on a real device upload against local Supabase (2026-09-21): a
16.1 MB clip landed with status=ready and duration_seconds NULL.

## Both halves already exist, nothing connects them

- The mutation ACCEPTS it: packages/shared/src/api/mutations.ts:641 declares
  `durationSeconds?: number`, and writes it on INSERT (:684) and UPDATE (:731),
  each guarded by `!= null`.
- The recorder KNOWS it: apps/mobile/lib/video/use-video-recorder.ts:433
  computes `elapsedMs` from `recordStartedAtRef` and already uses it for
  cap-vs-interruption classification at :436.

A grep for `durationSeconds` across apps/mobile/lib/video/ and
apps/web/hooks/use-video-recorder.ts returns nothing. Neither client passes it.

## Why it matters

duration_seconds is read and returned by four backend RPCs
(get_athlete_videos, get_match_details, get_match_videos, get_athlete_stills),
so every video list row ships a NULL. It is also the natural field for a
playback UI to show length before load, and for anything sizing analysis work.

Note the column has NO CHECK constraint and is client-supplied, so it is
trusted input. Prefer the recorder's measured elapsed time over anything
user-editable, and consider whether the value should be sanity-bounded on
write given matches.duration_seconds is constrained to 0 < n <= 3600 while
match_videos.duration_seconds is not.

## Scope

- Pass the measured duration from the mobile recorder through
  startMatchVideoUpload into the existing mutation param.
- Same for web (MediaRecorder can report it, or take it from the resulting
  blob via a <video> element the way scripts/test-video/viewer/app.js already
  does at :400-415).
- On a resumed upload the duration must survive the resume, since the row is
  written after the bytes land and possibly in a later process.

Related: the same upload shipped thumbnail_url NULL, tracked separately.

title: Funnel persisted upload writes through one guarded helper
description:
The supersede model in video-upload-manager.ts is now guard-dense rather than
structurally safe: thirteen isCurrent() call sites, each sitting immediately
after the await that opens its window. It is correct today -- verified by
grep and pinned by 38 manager tests covering all five interleavings -- but it
is correct only while nobody adds a fourteenth await without a guard.

## Recommended shape

The implementer proposed a cancellation token threaded into uploadBytes and
writeRow. The reviewer proposed something cheaper with most of the benefit:
funnel every persisted write through a single guardedPatch(handle, matchId,
patch) helper that no-ops when superseded. That is a mechanical refactor a
reviewer can verify by counting call sites, rather than a rewrite of the
function that just carried three P0 races.

Prefer the helper unless the token buys something the helper does not.

## Why this was NOT done now

Explicitly considered and deferred during the review of 1587740. Rewriting
the exact function that just carried three reproduced P0s, before any device
testing has happened, trades a known-good tested state for an unknown one.
The reviewer's verdict was "ship the guard-dense version, do not block".

## Requirements when it lands

Same suite green (mobile 837+, video-path 125+), and its own independent
review pass. Do not let an implementer approve this one.

title: P2: failed match-video upload is terminal, invisible past the wizard, and strands the local file
description: The match-keyed upload store is read only inside MatchRecorderProvider, so once the user taps the summary exit CTA nothing renders it again. Store is in-memory only, there is no manual retry, and deleteAsync appears nowhere in apps/mobile so the recorded MP4 is never cleaned up on success or failure. Failure scenario: both upload attempts fail on gym wifi, the user exits within ~10s, the process is later killed, the video is permanently lost with no notice and a 300MB-1GB orphan in the app cache.
notes:
Confirmed in detail by the video implementer during 46fb344 and deliberately NOT fixed, because it needs a product decision. The match-keyed store is read only inside MatchRecorderProvider, so once the user taps the summary exit CTA nothing renders it again; the store is in-memory only; the single automatic retry inside handleUpload is the only retry anywhere; and deleteAsync appears nowhere in apps/mobile, so the recorded MP4 is never cleaned up on success OR failure. On a ladder night that is one orphaned multi-hundred-MB file per match plus recorded matches whose video silently does not exist. Wants persistence plus a visible retry affordance.
GROUNDWORK EXISTS as of 23590b3, committed but NOT authored in that session and NOT finished. Landed: tus-js-client ^4.3.1 (pure JS, OTA-eligible, does not force a TestFlight build), packages/shared/src/utils/backoff.ts (exponential backoff with EQUAL jitter, deliberately not full jitter because full can return ~0ms), apps/mobile/lib/video/upload-persistence.ts (AsyncStorage-backed unfinished-upload record, one record per match keyed on matchId which is safe because match_videos has uq_match_video_uploader, one AsyncStorage key per record so progress writes and the resume sweep cannot clobber each other, and a bytes-vs-row phase split so a job that finished uploading never re-uploads hundreds of MB to retry one INSERT), apps/mobile/lib/video/tus-rn-shims.ts, and a types shim for the tus browser deep import so Metro and Jest resolve the same file. NOT DONE: nothing consumes any of it (backoff.ts names lib/video/video-upload-manager.ts, which does not exist), and none of the three new source files has tests. The product decision on persistence plus a visible retry affordance is still open.
PM 2026-10-04: groundwork is now consumed (video-upload-manager.ts exists, jobs persist and resume). Visibility past the wizard -> jits-n2im.2, retry -> jits-n2im.3.

title: P2: drift guard defeatable by a selector list containing both a theme attribute and :root
description: tokens-mirror-drift.test.ts themeOf (~:395-403) returns on the first matching selector, so '[data-theme="light"], :root { --bg-primary: #F2F4F7 }' is classified light-only and never merges into the dark palette, while real CSS applies it to :root too.
